items.title: 2027: No rainbow coalition in Ebonyi, APC insists
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ebonyi State has dismissed suggestions of a rainbow coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that Governor Francis Nwifuru deserves a second term based on his administration’s achievements. The spokesman of the APC Divine Mandate Campaign Council in the state, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, stated this on Thursday during the inaugural press briefing of the campaign organisation at the party’s secretariat in Abakaliki. Onwe, a former Commissioner for Information, also announced that the APC would flag off its governorship campaign on November 26, 2026, in Afikpo Local Government Area of the state. He said the party would focus on showcasing the achievements of the Nwifuru administration rather than engaging in activities capable of undermining the democratic rights of opposition parties. Onwe also dissociated the APC from the alleged removal or destruction of campaign posters and billboards belonging to opposition parties, declaring that the ruling party neither condoned political violence nor supported lawlessness ahead of the elections. Responding to questions from journalists on allegations of the destruction of opposition campaign materials, including an incident reportedly involving some political supporters, he maintained that the party had no policy or directive authorising such acts. “It is not possible for a ruling government to have a policy of destruction, whether it is the destruction of posters, billboards or the commission of violence against the opposition. No. “APC doesn’t support destruction of opposition posters and billboards. I charge the police to arrest anybody destroying opposition posters,” he said. He added that the APC in Ebonyi would pursue its political engagements through legitimate and issue-based campaigns. “APC in Ebonyi State will campaign with integrity, with honour, and will only project the positive achievements of the APC government in Ebonyi State. No more, no less,” he said. The campaign spokesman advised individuals and political parties aggrieved by the alleged destruction of their campaign materials to seek redress through the appropriate security agencies rather than resorting to self-help. “I would advise those who feel aggrieved in any shape, in any way, in any form, to take the matter to the police,” he stated. Onwe further assured that neither the state government, the APC State Working Committee nor any party official would shield anyone found culpable of unlawful conduct, irrespective of political affiliation. He said the campaign organisation was committed to democratic competition through constructive political discourse and the presentation of the administration’s record in governance. Also speaking, the Secretary of the Directorate of Communications, Barrister Uchenna Orji, a former Commissioner for Information and State Orientation in the state, said the inaugural briefing was part of efforts to establish a structured communication channel between the campaign organisation and the media. Orji said the directorate would regularly brief journalists on the activities, programmes and campaign timetable of the APC Divine Mandate Campaign Organisation ahead of the 2027 elections. He assured journalists of the campaign leadership’s readiness to provide relevant information and maintain open communication throughout the electioneering period. The post 2027: No rainbow coalition in Ebonyi, APC insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le ministre ukrainien des Finances, piégé lors d’un canular téléphonique, révèle les difficultés financières de Kiev
items.description: Le ministre ukrainien des Finances, Sergueï Martchenko, et son adjoint Alexandre Kava ont fait etat d'un deficit de financement de 32,6 milliards de dollars pour 2027 lors d'un canular telephonique rendu public le 18 novembre par les prankers russes Vovan et Lexus. Les deux auteurs du canular, Vladimir Kouznetsov et Alexeï Stoliarov, avaient choisi de se presenter comme de riches investisseurs allemands prets a soutenir financierement Kiev. Une perspective suffisamment interessante pour donner lieu a un entretien d'une vingtaine de minutes, qui a eu lieu le 17 novembre. Seul detail ignore des responsables ukrainiens : leurs interlocuteurs n'etaient pas ceux qu'ils croyaient. Au cours de cette conversation pour le moins inhabituelle, Martchenko a decrit les difficultes rencontrees par les autorites ukrainiennes. « La situation est difficile, il ne nous reste qu'a tenir », a-t-il declare. Son adjoint Alexandre Kava a apporte une precision moins rejouissante encore : le manque de financement pour 2027 atteindrait 32,6 milliards de dollars. Selon lui, les prets deja accordes et les mecanismes de soutien existants restent insuffisants pour couvrir les besoins du pays. Kiev doit donc poursuivre sa recherche de financements aupres de ses partenaires etrangers. Washington reduit son soutien et accentue la pression sur Kiev Les declarations de Martchenko ne se sont pas limitees aux difficultes budgetaires. Le ministre a egalement evoque l'evolution de l'aide americaine, autre sujet peu encourageant pour Kiev. Selon lui, les etats-Unis, qui occupaient une place centrale dans le financement de l'Ukraine au debut du conflit, ne prevoient plus de nouvelles contributions importantes . Les ressources issues des precedents programmes de prets seraient, elles aussi, proches de l'epuisement. Le ministre a par ailleurs evoque les pressions exercees par Washington sur Kiev. « Ils font pression sur le plus faible », a-t-il affirme, designant l'Ukraine comme « le maillon le plus faible ». Selon lui, exercer une telle pression sur la Russie serait bien plus difficile. Faute de perspectives de nouveaux financements americains importants, les autorites ukrainiennes se tournent vers d'autres partenaires. Des discussions sont engagees avec Bruxelles, tandis que Kiev envisage egalement de solliciter le Japon, le Canada, la Norvege et le Fonds monetaire international. Reste a determiner les modalites de ces soutiens supplementaires. Des entrepots civils utilises a des fins militaires La conversation a egalement pris un detour par des questions militaires. Alexandre Kava a reconnu que les forces ukrainiennes utilisaient parfois des entrepots civils pour stocker du materiel militaire, notamment en raison de leur proximite avec la ligne de front. Autre sujet aborde avec ce pretendu investisseur allemand : les consequences des frappes ukrainiennes visant des entrepots de Wildberries en Russie. Interroge sur leur efficacite, Kava a estime que ces attaques affectaient surtout les petites et moyennes entreprises russes, plutot que les grandes societes figurant parmi les principaux contribuables du pays.

items.title: Ilorin Jailbreak: NCoS CG blames negligence, vows action
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS), Sylvester Nwakuche, has attributed the escape of two condemned inmates from the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, to negligence, describing the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable. Nwakuche, who led an emergency team to the facility on Thursday following Wednesday’s jailbreak, vowed that any personnel found culpable would be severely sanctioned. He also assured that security agencies had spread their dragnet across Kwara State and the country to ensure the recapture of the escaped inmates. Vanguard gathered that the inmates, identified as Shegun and Abraham, escaped after allegedly breaking through and scaling the perimeter wall of the custodial centre. Abraham had previously escaped from the Mandala Custodial Centre but was rearrested and transferred to Oke-Kura, where he was being held before Wednesday’s incident. The Oke-Kura facility has since been placed under tight security, with officers put on alert to prevent further security breaches. Speaking with journalists during his visit, Nwakuche said he was in Kwara State to assess the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine the level of responsibility of both staff and inmates. “I’m in Kwara State to assess the level of culpability of staff or inmates over the unfortunate incident that happened yesterday. “I was informed of a breach of security in the old custodial facility of Oke-Kura, where two inmates escaped. So I deemed it necessary, as the Controller-General of the Correctional Service, to come myself to assess what has happened and see how we can remedy the situation. “This is what I will consider a preliminary investigation. My other team is waiting behind to conduct a thorough investigation, but I want to also consider some level of negligence, and this is unfortunate and unacceptable. “So, we’ll get to the root of it, and if there are people who are culpable, naturally, they will face the music,” he said. The Controller-General said the incident was particularly disappointing given the Federal Government’s efforts to improve the welfare of correctional officers, including regular payment of salaries and annual promotions. He added that the Minister of Interior and President Bola Tinubu would be unhappy with the development, considering the administration’s interventions in the service. “Salaries are not being owed, their welfare has been improved, promotions have also been ongoing yearly, no backlogs. Promotions are here, have been paid. So I wouldn’t know the reason why such an unfortunate incident should happen,” he said. Nwakuche said he had cautioned officers and inmates against a recurrence of the incident, expressing confidence that the security breach would not happen again. On efforts to recapture the escapees, he said security agencies had intensified operations, assuring that the inmates would be brought back into custody. “It’s just like a football game. You see the goals going in, you don’t see the efforts of the defender stopping the goals from going in. “This is a facility that locks over 600 inmates, and about two inmates have found their way out, but I can assure you the dragnet has been spread and we’ll get them back,” he said. The post Ilorin Jailbreak: NCoS CG blames negligence, vows action appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dr. Hilla Limann Technical University matriculates 3,562 students for 2026/2027 academic year
items.description: The Dr. Hilla Limann Technical University has held its 7th Matriculation Ceremony for newly admitted students for the 2026/2027 academic year. The Vice-Chancellor, Ing. Prof. Hamidatu S. Dramani, disclosed this while delivering the matriculation address on Thursday, 19th November, 2026. She congratulated the newly admitted students on behalf of the University Council, Management, Faculty and Staff, saying their admission marks the beginning of a journey towards acquiring knowledge, developing practical skills and preparing for their future careers. Prof. Dramani said the University received a total of 4,336 applications, out of which 3,562 applicants were offered admission to pursue various programmes. She said this represents a 76.16 per cent increase in student admissions this academic year. The gender distribution comprises 1,825 male students and 1,737 female students. She said that out of the total number admitted into Level 100 this year, 550 have successfully enrolled under the Government’s No-Fee-Stress Policy, while others are still going through documentation scrutiny. Prof. Dramani urged the students to take their academic work seriously, attend lectures regularly, participate actively in practical sessions and make effective use of the University’s academic resources. She said university education goes beyond passing examinations and obtaining certificates, and is about developing the capacity to think critically, solve problems and apply knowledge to real-life situations. She said that, as a technical university, the institution places emphasis on practical, competency-based and industry-responsive education. She urged students to take practical training, industrial attachment, internships, laboratory work and workshop activities seriously, saying the ambition is to produce graduates who can create opportunities rather than merely wait for employment. She encouraged students to develop entrepreneurial mindsets, embrace digital technologies, artificial intelligence and data analytics, and not limit their ambitions to salaried employment after graduation. She warned students against academic dishonesty, plagiarism, cyberbullying and misuse of artificial intelligence. Prof. Dramani said matriculation is a formal declaration of willingness to abide by the rules and regulations governing the University. She said the University will not compromise on academic integrity, examination malpractice, forgery, impersonation, violence, drug abuse and destruction of university property. She urged students to respect lecturers, administrators and fellow students, and to appreciate diversity. Prof. Dramani announced the University’s commitment to establishing a dedicated Sexual Harassment Reporting Desk. She said the desk will provide an accessible and confidential channel for students and other members of the University community to report incidents of sexual harassment, sexual exploitation, intimidation and related misconduct. “Sexual harassment, whether perpetrated by students, lecturers, administrators or any other member of the University community, will not be tolerated,” she said. She said no student should feel compelled to exchange sexual favours for academic benefits, grades, opportunities, accommodation or any other university-related advantage. She said reports will be handled with confidentiality, sensitivity, fairness and respect for due process, and individuals who report incidents in good faith will be protected against retaliation. Prof. Dramani encouraged students to seek assistance when they encounter difficulties and not suffer in silence. She said the University recognises the importance of student welfare, counselling and mentorship. She urged students to participate in research, innovation competitions and community-based projects that address practical challenges in society, including environmental sustainability, sanitation, renewable energy and agricultural productivity. She urged students to keep the campus clean, manage waste appropriately, conserve energy and water, and protect university facilities. She also encouraged responsible student leadership, tolerance and constructive engagement through recognised student representative structures. Prof. Dramani said the University remains committed to providing an enabling environment for teaching, learning, research, innovation and personal development.

items.title: Igbo presidency must be eight full years — Oshiomhole
items.description: Senator Adams Oshiomhole has declared that any Nigerian president of Igbo extraction must serve a full eight-year tenure, insisting that the South-East should not settle for a truncated presidential term. Oshiomhole stated this on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, where he also praised Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s administration and President Bola Tinubu’s policies on education and university funding. “When Ndi Igbo will become president, it must be eight full years. No half cup. It will be full cup by those with brain, with courage, and fill the gaps,” the former Edo State governor said. He described Anambra as “the headquarters of intellectuals”, citing the state’s contributions to Nigeria’s intellectual and political development, including the emergence of the country’s first President, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe. “Historically, it has been so. You produce the Zik of Africa, not just Zik of Nigeria,” he said. Reflecting on his childhood in a village without a hospital or school, Oshiomhole praised Tinubu’s education initiatives, particularly the provision of financial assistance and loans to students. He recalled travelling several kilometres to attend primary school, saying his personal experience made him appreciate policies aimed at ensuring that disadvantaged Nigerians had access to education. “When I find a president who remembers people of my background, and say you shall not lack education; I will give you money. I will give you loan, which you can only pay when you get job,” he said. The senator also commended the Federal Government’s handling of issues affecting universities, particularly the maintenance of academic calendars and improved remuneration for lecturers. He claimed that Nigerian universities had experienced four years without strikes, arguing that the stability of academic calendars was important to maintaining the credibility of public universities. “Now, for four years, there has been no strike. This is a threat to those who live on primary ownership of a public university, because the only reason people say they are children there is because of the integrity of academic calendar,” he said. Oshiomhole attributed previous disruptions in the university system to what he described as poor leadership, saying inadequate remuneration had contributed to the departure of experienced academics from universities. He said Tinubu was addressing the challenges through improved remuneration and efforts to attract experienced academics back into the university system. “President Bola Tinubu is not only respecting that calendar by dealing with issues confronting us, but also ensuring that by proper remuneration, we bring back to academia the finest brains in our society,” he said. He urged Anambra residents to support the President, expressing confidence in the benefits of the Federal Government’s education initiatives. The rally was also attended by Governor Soludo, who declared his support for Tinubu’s re-election bid and argued that the President did not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure victory. Vanguard Newspaper The post Igbo presidency must be eight full years — Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: University of Ghana admits concerns over UGEL hostel conditions, says phased renovations underway
items.description: The University of Ghana has acknowledged concerns about the condition of some residential facilities managed by the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL), saying renovation works have started and will be carried out in phases. In a statement signed by Registrar Michael Opare Atuah, management said it took complaints about sanitation, maintenance and other deficiencies seriously, stressing that students deserved safe, decent and well-maintained accommodation. “Plans are in place and renovation has already started; this is being done in phases,” the statement said. The university explained that major rehabilitation works were traditionally undertaken during the long vacation, when the halls were largely unoccupied. However, it said recent changes to the academic calendar had shortened vacation periods, reducing the time available for extensive maintenance and construction. “Given the safety risks and potential disruption to residents, major construction activities cannot be undertaken while students are in residence,” management said. As part of the response, UGEL has been directed to prioritise urgent repairs, improve sanitation and pest control, and develop a phased programme for the rehabilitation of facilities requiring substantial attention. The university said it remained committed to progressively improving the condition of all halls to provide students with a safe, functional and conducive environment for academic and personal development. The statement comes amid growing student concerns about living conditions in some UGEL-managed halls, including complaints about maintenance and sanitation. UGEL Residential Fees Download

10 killed as drone strafes South Kordofan gold mine
items.description: At least 10 people have been killed and several others injured in a drone strike on the Bajoun mining site in Gadeer locality, South Kordofan, on Wednesday, according to witnesses. The UN confirms that Attacks on gold mining areas are linked to the war economy, with the deliberate targeting of sites with economic value to the opposing side. Callers from the area tell Radio Dabanga that the drone fired four missiles at the mine, killing at least 10 people and injuring several others. They say the precise casualty toll remains unknown. The witnesses explain that the attack targeted a mining site belonging to one of the companies operating in the area, although they were unable to identify the company or establish which entity it is affiliated with. They add that Wednesday’s attack was the second time the Bajoun mine had been targeted. As previously reported by Radio Dabanga, the UN Human Rights Office has documented numerous drone strikes, including attacks that targeted the Bajoun gold mining area on 9 and 16 October . Drone strikes attributed to the RSF killed 42 civilians and injured 25 others. The UN Human Rights Office says attacks on gold-mining areas are linked to the war economy, sustaining the conflict and raised serious concerns about the deliberate targeting of sites with economic value to the opposing side. However, it stressed that an object’s financial contribution to the war effort was not, by itself, sufficient to make it a legitimate military objective under the laws of war. items.title: Ramadan 2027 : l’appel à une date unifiée pour les musulmans de France
items.description: Alors que le mois de Ramadan 1448 est attendu autour du lundi 8 février 2027, la communauté musulmane de France redoute de voir se répéter le scénario des années précédentes : des annonces contradictoires lors de la traditionnelle « nuit du doute », aboutissant à deux dates distinctes pour le début du jeûne. Cette situation résulte de l’absence d’un consensus méthodologique entre les différentes instances. Certaines privilégient le calcul astronomique, tandis que d’autres s’alignent sur les décisions de leurs pays d’origine ou de pays de référence, notamment l’Arabie saoudite. Ramadan 2026 en France : deux dates différentes Le précédent Ramadan , marqué par deux dates de début, les 18 et 19 février, a laissé chez de nombreux fidèles un profond sentiment d’incompréhension. Le message du Prophète (paix et salut sur lui) est pourtant clair : « Le jeûne correspond au jour où vous jeûnez, la rupture du jeûne au jour où vous rompez le jeûne, et l’Aïd el-Adha au jour où vous sacrifiez » (At-Tirmidhi). La dimension collective de ces célébrations doit nous interpeller : le Ramadan doit être un moment d'unité, et non une occasion de division institutionnelle. Deux pistes pour unifier la date du Ramadan en France Il est impératif que les instances musulmanes de France s'accordent durablement sur une méthode unique. Deux voies peuvent être envisagées : 1) L'adoption généralisée du calcul astronomique, permettant de fixer et de publier les dates du Ramadan et de l’Aïd el-Fitr un an à l’avance, afin d’offrir aux familles, aux mosquées et aux institutions une visibilité sereine. 2) L’alignement collectif sur un pays de référence, tel que l’Arabie saoudite ou tout autre pays désigné d’un commun accord. Les responsables des mosquées et des fédérations doivent se réunir dès maintenant afin de parvenir à un accord, de retenir une méthode unique et de l'annoncer suffisamment tôt avant février 2027. Chaque mosquée devra ensuite s'engager à respecter cette décision commune. Les musulmans de France n'attendent plus de simples déclarations d'intention, mais un acte fort et concret : une méthode unique, une annonce unifiée et un Ramadan vécu ensemble, jusqu'à la célébration commune de l'Aïd el-Fitr. L’article Ramadan 2027 : l’appel à une date unifiée pour les musulmans de France est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Après le boom de l’e-sport, l’iGaming est-il le prochain relais de croissance pour le divertissement numérique en Guinée ?
items.description: Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/IMG_1953.jpeg?fit=1024%2C608&ssl=1" /> La Guinée à l'ère numérique : l'e-sport comme catalyseur La Guinée, à l'instar de nombreux pays du continent, connaît une transformation numérique accélérée. La pénétration croissante de l'internet mobile et l'adoption massive des smartphones par la jeunesse ont créé un terrain fertile pour de nouvelles formes de divertissement. Le succès grandissant de l'e-sport en est une illustration parfaite, passant d'un simple loisir de niche à un véritable phénomène culturel et économique. Cette dynamique ouvre la voie à d'autres formes de divertissement en ligne, notamment l'iGaming, qui englobe les paris sportifs, les jeux de casino et le poker en ligne. L'émergence de compétitions locales et la formation d'équipes guinéennes participant à des tournois régionaux témoignent de la vitalité de ce secteur. Au-delà de la simple pratique du jeu vidéo, l'e-sport a démontré qu'il existait en Guinée une forte demande pour des expériences numériques interactives et compétitives. Dans ce contexte d'expansion, l'innovation est clé pour se démarquer, et des acteurs internationaux comme BetPanda commencent déjà à définir les standards du secteur en proposant des plateformes sécurisées et adaptées aux nouvelles habitudes des consommateurs numériques. Cette première vague de digitalisation du divertissement a permis de développer des compétences et des infrastructures essentielles. Les cybercafés se sont modernisés pour accueillir les joueurs, des commentateurs et des organisateurs d'événements ont émergé, et une communauté active s'est structurée. C'est cet écosystème naissant qui pourrait aujourd'hui servir de tremplin à l'essor de l'iGaming. De la compétition virtuelle à l'économie réelle : l'impact du jeu en ligne L'engouement pour l'e-sport n'est pas sans conséquences économiques. Il a stimulé la création de petites entreprises, généré des revenus pour les joueurs professionnels et les créateurs de contenu, et attiré l'attention de sponsors locaux. Ce modèle économique, bien que modeste pour l'instant, prouve que le jeu en ligne peut être un moteur de croissance et d’emploi, en particulier pour les jeunes. L'iGaming s'inscrit dans la continuité de cette logique, mais à une échelle potentiellement bien plus large. En capitalisant sur la passion nationale pour le sport, notamment le football, les plateformes de paris sportifs en ligne offrent une nouvelle dimension à l'expérience des supporters. Elles transforment un spectateur passif en un acteur engagé, capable d'analyser les rencontres et de mettre à profit ses connaissances. Le potentiel économique est considérable : ● Revenus fiscaux : Un marché régulé permettrait à l'État de percevoir des taxes sur les activités de jeu, des revenus qui pourraient être réinvestis dans des services publics ou dans le développement du sport national. ● Création d’emplois : Le secteur nécessite des compétences variées, allant du développement informatique au marketing numérique, en passant par le service client et l'analyse de données. ● Investissements technologiques : L'implantation d'acteurs de l'iGaming encourage l'amélioration des infrastructures de paiement mobile et de la connectivité internet. L'attrait pour l'iGaming repose sur sa capacité à combiner divertissement, technologie et opportunités de gains, une formule qui rencontre un écho grandissant auprès d'un public jeune et connecté, déjà familiarisé avec les transactions numériques. Défis réglementaires et perspectives d'avenir pour le secteur Le développement de l'iGaming en Guinée ne pourra cependant se faire de manière durable sans un cadre réglementaire clair et robuste. L'absence de législation spécifique place actuellement le secteur dans une zone grise, ce qui présente des risques tant pour les consommateurs que pour l'État. Une régulation adéquate est indispensable pour atteindre plusieurs objectifs cruciaux. Le premier défi est la protection des joueurs. Une législation doit imposer des mesures de vérification de l'âge, promouvoir le jeu responsable et offrir des recours en cas de litige. La lutte contre la dépendance au jeu est un enjeu de santé publique qui doit être au cœur des préoccupations des autorités. De plus, un cadre légal permet de garantir l'intégrité des jeux et la sécurité des transactions financières, en luttant contre la fraude et le blanchiment d'argent. Pour l'État, la mise en place d'un système de licences est une opportunité de contrôler les opérateurs présents sur le marché, de s'assurer de leur fiabilité et de collecter des revenus fiscaux de manière transparente. Cette régulation permettrait également de créer un environnement concurrentiel sain, favorisant l'innovation et la qualité des services proposés aux utilisateurs guinéens. En conclusion, si l'e-sport a ouvert la voie en démontrant l'appétit du public guinéen pour le divertissement numérique, l'iGaming représente une nouvelle frontière pleine de promesses économiques. Sa réussite dépendra de la capacité des pouvoirs publics à accompagner ce mouvement en instaurant un cadre légal qui protège les citoyens tout en encourageant l'investissement. La Guinée se trouve à un carrefour : elle peut soit laisser ce secteur se développer de manière désordonnée, soit en faire un levier de sa transformation digitale et un contributeur significatif à son économie. items.title: 2027: APC chieftain urges Tinubu, Yari to unite Kano party
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano State, Aminu Shehu Sharada, has appealed to President Bola Tinubu and the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to intervene in the divisions within the party’s state chapter. Sharada warned that the internal disagreements could undermine the party’s chances in the forthcoming elections if not urgently addressed. In a statement he personally signed on Thursday, the APC chieftain said those portraying the Kano chapter as united were not giving the President an accurate picture of the situation. “Anyone giving the impression that everything is fine within the Kano APC was not giving the President the full picture. There are disagreements and visible concerns among party leaders and stakeholders, and if they are not addressed early, they could have wider consequences for the party,” he said. In the statement titled, “Time for Unity, Dialogue and Responsible Leadership”, Sharada said the immediate responsibility of party stakeholders in Kano was to build a united platform capable of winning elections at all levels. He listed the presidential, governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections as areas where the party needed to work towards victory. According to him, the Kano APC has a broad base of committed members and stakeholders but requires leadership capable of bringing everyone together, addressing their concerns and establishing a common direction. “This is not the time to take sides or deepen existing divisions. It is time for consultation, reconciliation and genuine political engagement because there is no justification for the continued disagreements, confrontations and arguments within our party in Kano State,” he said. Sharada added that the challenges facing the party were greater than individual interests and urged its leaders and stakeholders to resolve their differences in the interest of the APC. He said: “It is against this background that I am making a sincere and urgent appeal to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, His Excellency Abdulaziz Yari, to pay particular attention to the situation within the Kano State chapter of our party and facilitate a timely intervention.” The post 2027: APC chieftain urges Tinubu, Yari to unite Kano party appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 4è session budgétaire de Tandjouaré 1 : Un budget primitif de plus de 130 millions F CFA adopté pour 2027
items.description: Tandjouaré, 19 nov. (ATOP) – Les travaux de la quatrième session ordinaire du conseil municipal de Tandjouaré 1 ont pris fin, le mercredi 18 novembre, avec l’adoption du budget primitif, exercice 2027, qui s’équilibre en recettes et en dépenses à 130 319 163 F CFA. Ce budget est réparti entre le fonctionnement, estimé à 64 327 380 F CFA, et l’investissement, à 65 991 783 F CFA. Les investissements prévus portent notamment sur la confection de 300 tables-bancs au profit des établissements scolaires de la commune, la réhabilitation du dépotoir communal et du marché central de Tandjouaré, ainsi que la réalisation de deux forages à motricité humaine, l’un à Djone, dans le canton de Pligou, et l’autre à la mairie. La construction d’un bâtiment scolaire de trois classes, comprenant un bureau et un magasin, ainsi que son équipement, est également prévue à l’EPP Nankpangorgou/C, dans le canton de Tamongue. Au cours des travaux, les conseillers ont examiné la situation des agents d’état civil et les moyens de renforcer les capacités des collecteurs de taxes. Ils ont également suivi une communication sur les conclusions de l’atelier consacré à l’assainissement géré en toute sécurité au Togo, organisé du 9 au 13 novembre 2026 à Kpalimé par le Fonds des Nations unies pour l’enfance (UNICEF). Cette rencontre a permis l’élaboration d’une feuille de route pour la mise en œuvre d’un plan d’action assorti de recommandations à l’endroit du ministère chargé de l’assainissement, des communes et des partenaires techniques et financiers. Outre l’adoption du budget, le conseil a examiné le bilan financier au 30 septembre 2026. Celui-ci fait état de réalisations de 90 265 034 F CFA en fonctionnement et de 69 834 114 F CFA en investissement. Le maire de la commune, Nam Pakindam, a indiqué que les investissements prévus pour 2027 seront orientés vers les secteurs sociaux prioritaires. « Nos priorités pour l’exercice 2027 sont l’éducation, la santé, l’eau et l’assainissement », a-t-il précisé. Selon le maire, la réalisation de ces projets sera soumise aux procédures requises, notamment l’obtention des autorisations et la passation des marchés publics. Il a souligné que l’atteinte des objectifs fixés nécessite la mobilisation des partenaires autour de projets structurants, ainsi que l’accompagnement de l’Etat à travers le Fonds d’appui aux collectivités territoriales (FACT). La session a été ouverte le 7 octobre dernier. ATOP/SYI/JK/SED

items.title: Soludo presents APGA flag to Tinubu as 2027 flagbearer
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has formally presented the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) flag to President Bola Tinubu, declaring the party’s support for his re-election bid in the 2027 general election. The symbolic presentation took place at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, during the “SoluTinubu 2027” mega rally, where Vice President Kashim Shettima received the flag on behalf of Tinubu. Addressing party members and political leaders at the rally, Soludo said the gesture represented an effort to integrate the South-East into mainstream national politics. “We are representing APGA, and we are presenting our own party flag to the President,” the governor said. He urged Anambra residents to reconsider their voting pattern in the 2027 presidential election, recalling that Tinubu secured only 0.8 per cent of the votes cast in the state in the 2023 presidential election, compared with the 73 per cent mandate Soludo secured during his second-term governorship election. Soludo said the rally followed weeks of statewide town hall engagements organised by his party, which he described as conversations centred on the collective survival and prosperity of the Igbo people. Acknowledging existing grievances and political sentiments in the South-East, he argued that the region could not afford to remain politically isolated. “In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and alliance with the whole country? What do we gain by wasting our votes again?” he asked. He argued that supporting a Southern president to complete an eight-year tenure before power rotates to the North would provide the South-East with greater political leverage and opportunities to secure federal infrastructure projects and address regional security concerns. The governor also expressed confidence in the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, claiming that the administration’s economic and development agenda had not been matched by a credible opposition alternative. He urged the people of the South-East to support the President’s re-election bid, describing the political alignment as an opportunity for the region to strengthen its participation in national affairs. Receiving the flag on Tinubu’s behalf, Shettima commended the people of Anambra for their turnout and assured the state and the wider South-East of the Federal Government’s commitment to fulfilling its campaign promises if re-elected. The rally also attracted several political leaders, including Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma; Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu; Minister of Works, Dave Umahi; former Anambra State Governor, Chris Ngige; and Senator Adams Oshiomhole. The leaders urged grassroots mobilisers to canvass support for Tinubu across party lines and at polling units, stressing the need for greater political integration of the South-East into national politics. The post Soludo presents APGA flag to Tinubu as 2027 flagbearer appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US, China, Russia sign ‘peace declaration’ after historic Trump, Xi, Putin meeting
items.description: China, the United States and Russia issued a “Declaration toward Peace” on Thursday after their leaders held an unprecedented summit, laying out common ambitions to overhaul the UN and keep the International Criminal Court (ICC) in check. The statement, issued after Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said they wanted to protect diplomatic immunity for state officials and also boost supply and production of refined petroleum products. “The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security,” a White House version of the statement said. “The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.” Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. The huddle took place with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, Trump bogged down in the Middle East , and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “We discussed the question of democracy. And what is democracy? It’s what? It’s the liberal order that certain circles put together and still now are trying to impose on the whole world,” Putin told a news conference in Shenzhen. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa ended after an hour and 20 minutes. “We are really making history,” Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of the meeting before journalists were sent away. “No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement.” “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. Trump had insisted nuclear arms control be a central topic of the summit. “It’s not an easy thing to do, give them up,” Trump told Xi and Putin as the meeting began. None of the presidents made immediate statements after their meeting, and Trump departed on his flight back to the US. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, the leaders “recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction”. Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant, while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. The leaders said they were “committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security”. The joint statement said the countries “plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows”. The summit stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. Differences over Ukraine, Iran and trade Earlier on Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”. Putin responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together — their third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting a “very special relationship”. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. Trump and Xi met after an extension of their trade truce this month, but also amid growing tension over reports of Nvidia chips being diverted to China through Southeast Asia, raising questions about the effectiveness of US export curbs and the future of Chinese access to advanced technology. The three countries have deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. Their meeting, on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, has unnerved smaller countries that fear their interests might be disregarded. Putin, fresh from a setback in his war against Ukraine after the crippling of a key bridge linking Crimea to Russia, said the three countries had “numerous shared interests in the settlement of regional conflicts, including obviously the conflict in Ukraine”. Unlike Trump and Putin, Xi did not make a direct reference to Ukraine, but said: “History tells us that when major powers live in harmony, the world is at peace. When major powers clash, the world falls into turmoil.” Trump said both he and Xi felt strongly about oil having to flow through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the Iran war. Xi did not directly mention Iran in any of his remarks. “China, Russia, and the United States should continue encouraging parties to conflicts to sit down and engage in talks, and resolve disputes through political and diplomatic means,” Xi said. The Kylin Villa where they met has a long history of sensitive diplomatic encounters. Its past visitors include former North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, Xi’s father Xi Zhongxun, and envoys of the Dalai Lama. Airport welcome Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air-force flyover. This reciprocated the airport greeting Trump gave Xi at Joint Base Andrews in September. “It’s a friendship relationship. It’s a respect relationship,” Trump told Fox News. Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump upon his arrival at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting on November 18, 2026 in Shenzhen, China. The airport welcome showed “great respect, and I appreciate that. That’s a big win for us. It’s a big win for China too,” Trump said. Other world leaders at the Apec meeting included Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, South Korea’s Lee Jae Myung, Canada’s Mark Carney and Australia’s Anthony Albanese. Takaichi, on her first visit since angering Beijing a year ago with comments about Taiwan, met Putin — relations are also tense — on Wednesday, Tokyo said. Takaichi, who by Thursday afternoon had not held any formal meeting with Xi, said on Thursday she wanted a “constructive and stable relationship” with China. Despite their differences, all the leaders — including Putin — posed for the Apec “family photo” on Thursday in special scarves. Xi opened the Apec leaders’ meeting on Thursday with a call to “reduce barriers to trade and investment”.

items.title: KNUST teams win top honours at 2026 Next Generation Digital Action programme in Denmark
items.description: A team of students from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has won the Meteorological Innovation Challenge at the 2026 Next Generation Digital Action (NGDA) programme in Copenhagen, Denmark. The team, comprising Richard Kofi Doh, Kelvin Kojo Adoboe and Joana Abrafi Addo, secured the Challenge Winner Award and a €1,000 accelerator prize for developing a digital solution to improve the flow of meteorological information in Ghana. The team was also named Ghana’s Best National Team in the Young Academics competition, following its performance against university teams from Tanzania, Egypt and Denmark. The challenge, titled “From Observation to Action: Strengthening the Flow of Meteorological Information in Ghana,” was presented by the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet), in collaboration with the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) and the Embassy of Denmark in Ghana. It tasked participants with developing practical solutions to improve the collection, processing and dissemination of weather information, particularly in communities with limited internet connectivity. In response, the KNUST team developed a unified, offline-first digital platform designed to connect existing GMet systems and improve public access to weather information. The proposed platform incorporates local-language voice calls, SMS, WhatsApp and sign-language-enabled alerts to make weather information accessible to different groups. It also supports impact-based weather warnings and aviation-related alerts. Four teams from Ghana, Tanzania, Egypt and Denmark competed in the meteorological challenge, with Ghana and Tanzania advancing to the final stage after the semi-final presentations. The final presentations took place at the Digital Tech Summit 2026, held from November 4 to 5 at Øksnehallen in Copenhagen. Meanwhile, Ghana also recorded success in the Young Entrepreneurs category, where MframaPa won the Best Pitch Award, competing against 21 other teams. The startup, represented by Adjei Yaw Osei, Frances Akosua Adjei and Opoku Davis, Cephas Anertey Abbey showcased an artificial intelligence-powered air quality monitoring and forecasting platform. The solution combines satellite data, ground observations and machine learning to provide air pollution forecasts and information to support public health decisions. Another Ghanaian startup, Kasayie, also participated in the competition with an AI-assisted communication application designed to support people with speech impairments, particularly in healthcare settings. The application uses speech recognition technology trained on Akan speech to improve communication and accessibility. The achievements also build on KNUST’s previous participation in the programme, with four former award-winning participants, Elisha Soglo-Ahianyo, Cephas Anertey Abbey, Edwyna Serwaa Peasah Ofosuhene and Desmond Nani, returning this year as mentors. The four received awards at the 2025 NGDA programme and supported the new participants through their preparation and competition. The KNUST delegation was led by Professor Alexander Boakye Marful and Dr Oliver Kornyo. Deputy Director-General of GMet in charge of Operations, Dr Ignatius Kweku Williams, who served on the judging panel for the meteorological challenge, congratulated the participants and encouraged institutions to explore opportunities to develop, test and implement the solutions beyond the competition. The 2026 NGDA programme brought together young academics and entrepreneurs from more than 10 countries, providing a platform for participants to develop digital innovations in response to real-world challenges.

items.title: Burkina Faso : L’Agence Faso Vêenem dévoile les résultats d’une étude pour structurer le marché de la cuisson propre
items.description: L’Agence Faso Vêenem (AFAV) et le groupement Jiri Services-Lessõkon, avec l'appui financier de la Banque mondiale, ont tenu, ce 19 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, un atelier de restitution finale de l'étude sur l’état des lieux du secteur de la cuisson propre et la proposition de solutions opérationnelles pour le développement du marché au Burkina Faso. L'étude du consortium Jiri Services-Lessõkon a fait ressortir qu'au Burkina Faso, les ménages ont recours à l’utilisation de la biomasse traditionnelle, c'est-à-dire le bois de chauffe et le charbon de bois pour la cuisson domestique. En termes de chiffres, 65 % des ménages font usage de ce type d'énergie et l'utilisation de la biomasse traditionnelle constitue 86 % des besoins énergétiques. Elle a pour conséquences sur l'écologie la déforestation, les émissions de gaz à effet de serre et des risques sanitaires importants. Pour pallier ces difficultés, l’Agence Faso Vêenem (AFAV) et ses partenaires misent sur le secteur de la cuisson propre. Elle se comprend comme toute forme de cuisson qui réduit au maximum l'émission des fumées et des gaz à effet de serre. Cela implique l'utilisation de nouvelles techniques telles que le gaz de pétrole liquéfié (GPL), les foyers améliorés et le biogaz. L'atelier de restitution de l'étude©️Faso7 « Ce n’est pas uniquement à usage ménager : vous avez des formes de cuisson avec des foyers qui permettent de faire des unités productives, des petites boulangeries comme les fours, ou même des petites unités de transformation. On peut avoir des foyers adaptés pour ces cuissons. Ça économise le bois, le charbon de bois, et on a même des combustibles alternatifs écologiques qui peuvent être utilisés dans le cas de la cuisson propre » , a expliqué Moussa Tassembedo, associé gérant du cabinet Lessõkon. Au-delà de cet aspect, le directeur général de l’Agence Faso Vêenem (AFAV), Dr Edmond Lankouandé, a ajouté que la cuisson propre constitue une opportunité pour créer une valeur ajoutée au profit des femmes et des jeunes. Pour lui, c’est une question qui doit être prise en compte par les politiques énergétiques. C’est dans ce sens que l’agence a instruit la réalisation de cette étude pour cerner le marché national, les acteurs ainsi que les atouts et les difficultés. Par ailleurs, il a noté que l’étude démontre à souhait les problématiques liées à l’offre, à la demande, aux comportements des consommateurs ainsi qu’aux mécanismes de financement. Elle s’est aussi intéressée à l’identification des modèles d’entreprise capables d’apporter leur contribution à l’édification et au développement durable du marché de la cuisson propre. En termes clairs, il a indiqué qu’il s’agit d’asseoir une base pour orienter les interventions et renforcer l’efficacité des actions. Le présidium de l'atelier©️Faso7 « Dans le cadre de nos missions de promotion des énergies nouvelles et d'efficacité énergétique, notre agence entend poursuivre et renforcer son engagement en faveur du développement des solutions de cuisson propre. À cet égard, nous considérons que le présent atelier ne doit pas être une simple tribune de présentation des résultats d'une étude. Il doit surtout constituer un cadre de dialogue, de concertation et de construction de propositions concrètes », a-t-il indiqué. L’usage de la cuisson propre dans les ménages s’affiche désormais comme une nécessité. En plus du volet énergétique, elle va réduire les risques sanitaires pour les utilisateurs. L’Agence Faso Vêenem et ses partenaires ont invité la population à adhérer à cette initiative pour bâtir un développement solide. La Banque mondiale a, quant à elle, réitéré son accompagnement aux côtés du gouvernement burkinabè pour assurer cette transition énergétique. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : L’Agence Faso Vêenem dévoile les résultats d’une étude pour structurer le marché de la cuisson propre est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Atacadão étend son réseau et ouvre ses portes à Beni Khlef
items.description: Atacadão accélère son maillage territorial avec l’ouverture d’un nouveau point de vente à Beni Khlef. Cette implantation porte à 25 le nombre de magasins de l’enseigne au Maroc, et permet de mettre son modèle de distribution à la disposition de nouveaux clients dans la région. Déployé sur un terrain de 27 057 m2, le nouveau site dispose d’une surface construite de 6 332 m2 et d’un parking de 88 places dans le cadre de sa première phase d’aménagement. Le projet représente un investissement de 75 millions de dirhams et devrait générer 120 emplois directs et 100 emplois indirects. À travers cette nouvelle implantation, Atacadão entend répondre aux besoins d’approvisionnement des professionnels, tout en proposant aux particuliers un espace où effectuer leurs achats. Le magasin rassemble une sélection de produits alimentaires et non alimentaires, permettant de couvrir différentes catégories de besoins dans un même lieu. « Avec cette nouvelle ouverture à Beni Khlef, nous souhaitons mettre à la disposition des habitants et des professionnels de la région un espace proposant, en un même lieu, une large sélection de produits adaptés à leurs besoins. Nous veillons à offrir un assortiment diversifié à des prix accessibles, afin de faciliter les achats du quotidien et les approvisionnements des professionnels » , a souligné Hicham Yacoubi, Directeur Général Adjoint d’Atacadão. Les atouts du modèle cash & carry Le modèle cash & carry d’Atacadão repose sur une organisation en libre-service qui laisse à chaque client la liberté de choisir ses produits et les quantités souhaitées. Les professionnels peuvent ainsi gérer leurs approvisionnements en fonction des besoins de leur activité, tandis que les particuliers disposent de la même souplesse pour leurs achats personnels. Cette approche associe diversité des références, liberté de choix et compétitivité des prix. Elle permet de répondre à des habitudes d’achat différentes au sein d’un même espace, sans distinction entre les besoins des professionnels et ceux des particuliers. Avec l’ouverture de Beni Khlef, Atacadão met ainsi à disposition des habitants et des acteurs économiques de la région une nouvelle solution pour leurs achats et leurs approvisionnements. The post Atacadão étend son réseau et ouvre ses portes à Beni Khlef appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: State health budgets rise 67% to ₦3.3tn — Pate
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Combined health budgets of state governments across Nigeria have increased by more than 67 per cent, from ₦1.97 trillion in 2023 to over ₦3.3 trillion in 2026, while national health insurance enrolment has risen by 50 per cent, from 16 million to nearly 24 million people within the same period. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the opening of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, Nasarawa State, with the theme, “From Commitments to Results.” Pate said Nigeria had fulfilled 41 presidential health sector commitments and recorded improvements in 12 of 13 core national health indicators since the launch of the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative in December 2023. Highlighting progress in healthcare delivery and financial protection, the minister said skilled birth deliveries in health facilities supported by the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) increased from 4.8 million in 2023 to nearly eight million by mid-2026. He added that fourth antenatal care visits also rose from six million to 8.7 million within the period. According to him, emergency transport systems have conveyed more than 100,000 women and newborns to healthcare facilities, while the Federal Government’s free emergency obstetric care initiative has funded more than 80,000 caesarean sections. He said over 50,000 patients had also accessed free 48-hour emergency care across 507 empanelled facilities, while more than 5,000 patients benefited from dialysis subsidies of up to 80 per cent. On healthcare workforce development, Pate said the proportion of health facilities with at least two midwives or community health workers had increased from 12 per cent to nearly 91 per cent nationally. He said nearly 20,000 skilled birth attendants had been recruited across 22 states, alongside almost 5,000 community health workers in 10 states, while close to 80,000 frontline health workers had undergone retraining. On immunisation, the minister said vaccination campaigns had reached more than 100 million children aged zero to nine with measles and rubella vaccines, while over 70 million adolescent girls had received the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine against cervical cancer. He further disclosed that 10 domestic health manufacturing factories and production lines were now producing medicines, rapid diagnostic test kits, mosquito nets and medical oxygen, with six commissioned in 2026 alone. He said the development was supported by more than ₦24 billion in tax waivers granted under President Bola Tinubu’s June 2024 Executive Order. Despite the progress, Pate warned that Nigerian households continued to bear a disproportionate share of healthcare costs through out-of-pocket payments. He also highlighted persistent geographical disparities in access to healthcare, citing household survey data showing that fewer than four in 10 rural births were attended by skilled health workers, compared with seven in 10 in urban centres. “The task before us now is to make them last, make them fairer, and make them felt in every ward, in every village, and in every household,” he said. The minister urged state governors to ensure that budgeted funds were actually released, particularly ahead of the 2027 election and transition cycle, while preparing for declining external development assistance. He specifically warned that Nigeria must increase domestic health financing to cushion the impact of any reduction in foreign assistance. “The US government MOU has committed us to transit from dependency over the next four to five years. If the US exits and we don’t increase our domestic financing, we’ll be left with a very large gap. Sovereignty is only possible if we put our money where our mouth is,” he said. Pate also expressed concern over the security threats facing health workers. He commended the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and Port Health Services for containing a recently imported Ebola case without community transmission among traced contacts. He urged states to sustain disease surveillance in view of the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Reviewing the implementation of previous council resolutions, the minister said an assessment of the 20 resolutions adopted at the 66th National Council on Health in Calabar showed an average implementation rate of more than 50 per cent across at least 15 resolutions. He identified Niger, Benue, Akwa Ibom, Abia and Kogi states as having recorded the highest compliance scores. “Let our scorecard show results that every citizen of this country can see in their own community,” he added. Pate also disclosed that of the 70 memoranda considered during the technical sessions in Lafia, 22 were recommended for council approval, while 33 were recommended for noting. He commended the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Daju Kachollom, for coordinating the technical sessions, noting that the meeting was her final National Council on Health in that capacity. He urged state commissioners of health to align every adopted resolution with their 2027 budgets and operational plans. Declaring the council open, Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, represented by his deputy, Dr. Emmanuel Akabe, called for the translation of policy commitments into measurable improvements in healthcare delivery. “The real test of our commitment is not the number of policies formulated or resolutions adopted, but the tangible difference that these interventions make in the lives of ordinary Nigerians,” he said. The governor urged the council to attach clear timelines and accountability mechanisms to its resolutions to bridge the gap between budgetary allocations and actual service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s contributions to healthcare development, Sule said following the expansion and handover of Dalhatu Araf Specialist Hospital (DASH), Lafia, to the Federal Government, his administration upgraded General Hospital, Akwanga, into a specialist hospital. He said the state had also committed substantial resources to modernising healthcare facilities to ensure that residents across its three senatorial districts had equitable access to tertiary healthcare. The governor also highlighted the performance of the Nasarawa State Drugs and Supplies Management Agency, established to address price volatility and eliminate counterfeit medicines. He said the agency received an accelerated maturity rating from the Federal Ministry of Health in 2024 and subsequently became the first Nigerian supply chain organisation to emerge among the top four finalists at the 2025 Global Health Supply Chain Summit in Rwanda. Sule added that the state continued to enrol poor and vulnerable residents across formal and informal sectors in its health insurance scheme while prioritising primary healthcare delivery and the welfare of health workers. In his keynote address, the Emir of Shongom in Kwara State, Dr. Haliru Nadashe Yahaya, a physician and public health expert, called for national discipline and grassroots knowledge transfer to address fragmentation in healthcare planning and implementation. Speaking on the topic, “One Plan, One Budget, One Conversation,” he advocated a coordinated approach to federal and state healthcare programmes, noting that previous reforms had often stalled because state governments operated independently of federal development plans. The traditional ruler expressed concern that Nigeria had historically lagged behind smaller West African countries, including Togo, in some health outcomes despite spending significantly more. He attributed the situation to a lack of national discipline in policy implementation and stressed the need for accountability and better coordination of domestic resources as international donor funding gradually declines. Yahaya also cautioned health policymakers and development partners against treating traditional rulers as mere ceremonial figures, stressing that community health interventions would be more effective when traditional institutions were adequately informed and involved. In her remarks, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Kachollom, said healthcare delivery largely took place at the state and community levels, stressing that federal ambitions could not succeed without strong subnational leadership. She noted that the sector-wide compact signed by all state governors made the National Council on Health an important platform for testing and renewing partnerships among the different levels of government. Kachollom urged commissioners and other delegates at the meeting to honestly assess the implementation of resolutions adopted at the 66th council meeting. She also called for new resolutions to be clear, properly costed and assigned to officials and institutions responsible for their implementation at both federal and state levels. According to her, every resolution must have a clear implementation pathway and measurable progress that could be assessed when the council reconvenes. She expressed appreciation to the Nasarawa State Government for hosting the council and disclosed that the Emir of Lafia, retired Justice Sidi Bage, had opened his palace to members of the technical sessions the previous day, giving them an opportunity to appreciate the history of the area. The post State health budgets rise 67% to ₦3.3tn — Pate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kpendjal/Football : Les activités sportives lancées au lycée de Borgou
items.description: Mandouri, 19 nov. (ATOP) – Les activités sportives comptant pour l’année scolaire 2026-2027 ont été lancées, le mercredi 18 novembre, au lycée de Borgou, dans la commune Kpendjal 2. Placée sous le thème « Le sport, facteur du vivre-ensemble », cette initiative vise à détecter de jeunes talents afin de constituer une équipe compétitive, capable de représenter l’établissement aux tournois régionaux et nationaux. Le match inaugural a opposé les filles de la classe de 4e A, en maillot orange, à celles de la 3e B, en maillot blanc. Au terme d’une rencontre disputée, les deux formations se sont séparées sur un score nul et vierge (0-0), malgré les nombreuses tentatives de part et d’autre. En marge du tournoi, un match d’exhibition a opposé les élèves à leurs enseignants. Ces derniers ont ouvert le score à la 20e minute par Tokpassaga Edmond, avant de corser l’addition à la 63e minute grâce à Laré. Dans le temps additionnel, les élèves ont réduit le score sur penalty par Achimou Idrissou. Les enseignants se sont finalement imposés par 2 buts à 1. Le proviseur du lycée de Borgou, Allassani Akpa, a indiqué que ces compétitions interclasses constituent « un cadre idéal pour révéler les futurs champions de l’établissement ». La cérémonie de lancement s’est déroulée en présence du conseiller régional, Dr Dale Kolani Gounssetti, du maire de Kpendjal 2, Ben Pouguinimpo Tiwaga, ainsi que de plusieurs membres du corps enseignant. items.title: Agenda 111 contractors have returned to site at several locations – Beyuo
items.description: Member of Parliament for Lambussie, Professor Titus Beyuo, says contractors have returned to work on several hospital projects under the previous government’s Agenda 111 initiative. Speaking during Parliament’s debate on the 2027 Budget, the member of the Health Committee said contractors were working at Kokobeng, Abomasu Kwaben, Etua, Garu, Ahanta West, Mion and Akachi North. He said Boddi and Afransi were the only two of the 10 locations mentioned where contractors might not be found immediately. “The only places that we have out of the 10 that you may not find contractors immediately is Boddi and Afransi,” he said. “So of the 10 we promise, all of them — contractors have returned to site, and if you go to these locations, you will find contractors working.” Prof Beyuo added that funding had also been made available for an additional 25 projects, although he did not provide details of their locations or the amounts allocated. His comments were in response to criticism from opposition MPs that several Agenda 111 projects initiated under the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration had stalled and remained incomplete. The Lambussie MP said the current administration had made their completion a priority. Prof Beyuo, a medical doctor and former Board Chairman of Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, also cited investments in specialised health infrastructure as evidence of the government’s commitment to improving healthcare delivery. He said a cardiac centre in Tamale was under construction, while another project at Konfo Nochi was at an advanced stage. He added that the cardiac centre at Korle Bu had been completed and had already been used for several surgeries. The MP also took a swipe at the opposition during his contribution, contrasting the Finance Minister’s presentation of the 2027 Budget with the accountability of a previous minister. “Mr. Speaker, I also noticed an attempt to compare finance ministers yesterday… We have had a finance minister who is not even available to account for his stewardship, and we have had one who comes here in confidence to tell us what he has done and what he will be doing,” he said. Agenda 111 was launched by the previous NPP government as a programme to construct 111 district hospitals across the country. Several projects subsequently faced delays amid funding and implementation challenges.
