items.title: Pakistan, Qatar reaffirm commitment to strengthening bilateral relations in security, counter-terrorism: ISPR
items.description: Pakistan and Qatar reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations in the areas of institutional cooperation, security and counter-terrorism on Thursday, the military’s media affairs wing said. The development cam as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir met with Qatar’s Interior Minister Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, who is currently visiting Pakistan, in Rawalpindi on Thursday, according to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). During the meeting, they discussed matters of mutual interest and the evolving regional and global security situation. They also discussed avenues for the enhancement of bilateral security cooperation, ISPR said. “Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries, particularly in the fields of security, counter-terrorism and institutional cooperation,” the statement said. The visiting dignitary appreciated Pakistan’s role in promoting regional peace and stability and acknowledged the longstanding fraternal ties between the two countries, it added. CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further deepen bilateral engagement with Qatar. He underscored the importance of close cooperation in addressing shared security challenges, the statement said. MoU signed on security cooperation The two countries earlier signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on security cooperation, along with an action plan to prevent drug smuggling. The MoU was signed between Qatar’s Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya) and the Federal Constabulary, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Qatari counterpart Al Thani signed the documents. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also witnessed the signing ceremony, the statement said. The PMO handout said that the premier “warmly” welcomed the visiting dignitary on “on his first visit to Pakistan and reaffirmed the longstanding brotherly relations between Pakistan and Qatar”. “He expressed the hope that the visit would further strengthen cooperation between the ministries of interior and relevant institutions of the two brotherly countries,” it said. PM Shehbaz also conveyed his greetings to the Qatari emir and thanked the country’s leadership for its “unwavering support to Pakistan”. “He particularly appreciated Qatar’s continued supply of liquefied natural gas, which contributes to meeting Pakistan’s energy requirements,” the statement said. PM Shehbaz highlighted that nearly 300,000 Pakistanis work in Qatar, where they play an important role in the country’s development and prosperity. He said that there were extensive opportunities to expand Pakistan-Qatar economic cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, agriculture, livestock, information technology and mining and minerals. The statement said that the Qatari minister thanked Pakistan for its hospitality. He also conveyed Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani’s congratulatory messages and best wishes to the prime minister. “He appreciated Pakistan’s role and efforts for promoting peace and stability in the region,” the statement added. According to a separate statement by the interior ministry, Naqvi and his counterpart also agreed to expand the scope of the exchange programme for police officers. The two also agreed to enhance cooperation between Qatar’s National Cyber Security Agency and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency. “A decision was made to improve coordination between the two interior ministries to enhance bilateral cooperation,” the statement said. It added that Qatar would also build a modern firing range at the National Police Academy. Naqvi thanked Qatar for providing the Anti-Narcotics Force with modern scanners, adding that “joint operations and information sharing” between the relevant agencies of the two countries were ongoing. “With joint cooperation between Pakistan and Qatar, 300 drug cases have been busted over the past four years,” Naqvi was quoted as saying. “We want to ensure that our territory is never used for drug smuggling,” the interior minister said. “Cybercrime is an international problem, and Pakistan is taking robust measures to combat it,” he added. Last month, in a meeting in Doha, Naqvi and the Qatari counterpart agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in internal security.

items.title: ONU : les Émirats mobilisent leur puissance financière pour imposer leur candidate
items.description: a l'approche de la succession d'António Guterres, les emirats arabes unis mobilisent leurs relations economiques pour soutenir Lana Nusseibeh . Selon Middle East Eye, des diplomates estiment que l'ancienne ambassadeur emiratie a l'ONU beneficie desormais de l'appui des membres permanents du Conseil de securite, seuls capables d'opposer leur veto. Aucun soutien unanime n'a toutefois ete officiellement confirme. Abou Dhabi dispose de puissants leviers. Aux etats-Unis, les emirats ont annonce en 2025 un programme d'investissements de 1 400 milliards de dollars sur dix ans, notamment dans l'intelligence artificielle et l'energie. Middle East Eye evoque en outre l'investissement de 500 millions de dollars d'un prince emirati dans une entreprise de cryptomonnaies liee a la famille Trump. Les emirats peuvent compter sur leurs investissements Avec Londres, les relations reposent sur pres de 30 milliards de dollars d'engagements d'investissement pour 2021-2026, mais aussi sur le football et l'immobilier. Selon le media, appuyer Lana Nusseibeh pourrait apaiser les tensions liees au dossier Manchester City. La France entretient des liens etroits avec Abou Dhabi : 10,8 milliards d'euros d'echanges commerciaux en 2025, cooperation militaire et contrats Rafale. La Russie a enregistre 20,4 milliards de dollars de commerce non petrolier avec les emirats en 2025. Quant a la Chine, ses echanges bilateraux hors hydrocarbures depassaient 111 milliards de dollars, tandis que les ports emiratis jouent un role majeur dans sa desserte regionale. L'influence se heurte toutefois au dossier soudanais . Abou Dhabi est accuse de soutenir les Forces de soutien rapide, responsables d'exactions massives, ce que les autorites emiraties dementent. Lana Nusseibeh a elle-meme rejete les accusations. Au Royaume-Uni, 66 parlementaires demandent au gouvernement de bloquer sa candidature. Un nouveau vote consultatif est prevu le 19 novembre. Au-dela du choix d'une secretaire generale, la campagne pose une question : jusqu'ou les partenariats economiques pesent-ils sur la gouvernance de l'ONU ?

Our support for the EMY Africa Awards reflects our commitment to celebrating individuals whose leadership, innovation and achievements continue to transform industries, empower communities and contribute meaningfully to Africa’s progress. items.title: INEC assures Nigerians of neutrality in 2027 elections
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has assured Nigerians of its neutrality and commitment to conducting credible 2027 general elections. The INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance on Thursday in Abuja, at the 2026 Annual Lecture and Awards of the Association of Corporate Online Editors (ACOE). The INEC chairman spoke on the theme: “Roadmap to 2027: Strengthening Electoral Security Through Collaboration between INEC, the Media, and Political Parties for Credible and Hitch-Free Elections”. Amupitan, represented by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Adebayo Oketola, said the commission would not serve as an appendage of any political party, whether in government or opposition. He also said that the commission remained committed to institutional neutrality, legal compliance and transparent administration of the electoral process. According to him, INEC has conducted four major off-cycle elections and 16 legislative by-elections since the current leadership assumed office in October 2025. He said the exercises provided opportunities to identify operational weaknesses, assess logistics and strengthen procedures ahead of the 2027 general elections. The INEC boss reiterated that the presidential and National Assembly elections would hold on Jan. 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections would take place on Feb. 6, 2027. He disclosed that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Nov. 28, 2026, across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. He revealed that the commission had strengthened its result-uploading and validation procedures to address concerns surrounding result transmission. He also explained that polling unit figures entered on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). He added that more than 1.6 million invalid, duplicate and deceased entries had been removed from the voter register. Amupitan further disclosed that the commission had procured 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. “INEC has reduced the number of voters assigned to each BVAS device from 1,250 to 850 to minimise accreditation delays. “The commission has also made provisions for 232,658 persons with disabilities registered to vote,” he said. On electoral security, the INEC chairman said, that the commission was working with the Office of the National Security Adviser and the Nigeria Police Force through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security. He said the collaboration would be extended to state, local government and registration area levels to protect electoral personnel, materials and voters. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation, synthetic voice cloning, manipulated videos and coordinated information manipulation as major threats to the 2027 elections. He called on online editors to partner with INEC in separating verified information from fabricated reports capable of triggering electoral tension. He noted that false reports about relocated polling units, manipulated election footage and premature results could undermine public confidence and discourage voter participation. He also cautioned political parties against campaign violence, intimidation and attacks on electoral officials and facilities. He said the Electoral Act 2026 prescribed penalties for abusive campaign speeches, incitement and the deployment of private armed guards and masquerades at political rallies. He therefore urged political party leaders to control their supporters and pursue electoral grievances through lawful channels rather than violence. The event was attended by the Managing Director of the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), Malam Ali Muhammad, represented by his Special Adviser on Editorial Matters, Mr Ephraims Sheyin, representatives of media organisations, including Arise News, online editors and members of ACOE. The event also featured the inauguration of ACOE magazine, and presentation of awards to deserving individuals. (NAN) The post INEC assures Nigerians of neutrality in 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Somalie : le président accuse les Émirats d'ingérence et de soutenir des groupes armés
items.description: La rupture entre Mogadiscio et Abou Dhabi s'aggrave. Dans une allocution televisee le 17 novembre, le president somalien Hassan Sheikh Mohamud a accuse les emirats arabes unis d'« ingerence » dans les affaires de son pays, leur reprochant de financer des groupes armes echappant au controle de l'etat federal. Selon lui, Abou Dhabi aurait etabli des bases et des forces militaires paralleles, et soutenu certaines administrations regionales contre Mogadiscio. Au cœur de ses accusations figurent aussi les ports de Berbera, Bosaso et Kismayo, ou des accords auraient ete conclus sans l'aval du gouvernement central. Ces installations occupent une position cle sur les routes commerciales de la region. Soutien de plus en plus officiel a l'independance du Somaliland Le president affirme que les emirats ont utilise Berbera, en janvier, pour faciliter le depart d'un chef de milice yemenite, sans autorisation somalienne. Il leur reproche en outre un role presume dans la reconnaissance du Somaliland par Israel, un territoire separatiste dont Mogadiscio revendique la souverainete. Ces accusations n'ont pas ete etablies de maniere independante. La crise n'est pas nouvelle. Le 12 janvier 2026, la Somalie a annule ses accords de cooperation securitaire, militaire et economique avec les emirats, puis interdit son espace aerien a leurs avions militaires et de fret. Une decision qui a accentue les tensions avec des autorites regionales entretenant leurs propres relations avec Abou Dhabi. Le 18 novembre, Anwar Gargash, conseiller diplomatique du president emirati, a rejete les accusations, les attribuant aux calculs politiques de Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. Le ministre somalien de la Defense a replique en affirmant qu'Abou Dhabi d'acheter des loyautes et alimente les conflits. Au-dela de l'affrontement diplomatique, ce bras de fer revele la competition pour l'influence dans la Corne de l'Afrique . Pour Mogadiscio, l'enjeu est de reprendre la maîtrise de ses forces armees et de ses ports, sans voir ses divisions nourrir de nouvelles guerres par procuration.

items.title: YANGO GROUP NOMME UN RESPONSABLE MONDIAL DE LA SÉCURITÉ AFIN DE PILOTER UNE STRATÉGIE UNIFIÉE EN MATIÈRE DE SÉCURITÉ SUR LʼENSEMBLE DE SES MARCHÉS
items.description: © Yango Roman Zemlyansky dirigera le renforcement et la diversification des technologies de sécurité, des normes opérationnelles et du partage des meilleures pratiques sur les marchés où Yango propose ses services de mobilité. Dubaï, le 17 novembre 2026 – Yango Group, entreprise technologique internationale basée à Dubaï, harmonise son approche de la sécurité dans ses services de mobilité, en mettant lʼaccent sur la prévention des risques, le déploiement des bonnes pratiques et lʼadaptation des technologies aux différents services de transport et aux conditions de circulation locales, notamment pour les services utilisant des motos et des tricycles en Afrique, en Amérique latine, en Asie du Sud, dans la région MENA et dans dʼautres régions. Roman Zemlyansky, nommé Responsable mondial de la sécurité des services de mobilité (Global Head of Safety), pilotera cette initiative en collaboration avec les équipes dirigeantes, les équipes produit et opérationnelles, ainsi que des partenaires externes, notamment des organisations spécialisées dans la sécurité routière et les autorités locales. Il sera chargé de définir la stratégie de sécurité de lʼentreprise dans ses services de mobilité, dʼétablir les priorités en matière de déploiement technologique et de guider lʼamélioration des normes de sécurité ainsi que leur application sur les différents marchés. « Nous développons nos activités de mobilité dans une perspective à long terme. Cela signifie que nous devons gagner la confiance des personnes qui utilisent nos services et des partenaires qui développent leurs activités avec nous. La nomination de Roman renforce la place de la sécurité dans notre stratégie de croissance, depuis les priorités liées aux produits jusquʼaux décisions opérationnelles sur chaque marché. Elle nous permet de bénéficier d'un leadership stratégique dédié afin de consolider les progrès déjà réalisés et de déployer davantage les pratiques efficaces à travers lʼensemble de nos activités », a déclaré Adeniyi Adebayo, Directeur général de Yango Ridetech et Chief Business Officer (CBO) de Yango Group. Renforcer les technologies préventives et les opérations Lʼune des principales priorités technologiques sera dʼélargir lʼutilisation de lʼintelligence artificielle (IA) afin de contribuer à la prévention des incidents, tout en poursuivant le déploiement de dispositifs avancés de suivi des itinéraires et de vérification dʼidentité dans les services de mobilité de Yango. Roman Zemlyansky travaillera avec les équipes produit et opérationnelles afin de définir les modalités dʼadaptation de ces technologies aux différents services de transport et aux spécificités de chaque marché. Il développera également les méthodes permettant à lʼentreprise dʼévaluer lʼefficacité des mesures de prévention, en complément du suivi des taux dʼincidents signalés. En sʼappuyant sur les protocoles de sécurité déjà établis, Roman Zemlyansky veillera à étendre les pratiques ayant fait leurs preuves sur certains marchés et à harmoniser davantage les procédures lorsque cela sera pertinent. Cela inclut lʼamélioration des méthodes dʼévaluation des incidents, de leur remontée aux équipes compétentes et de la coordination des interventions, tout en tenant compte des exigences réglementaires et des réalités locales. Lʼentreprise a déjà commencé à mesurer publiquement les résultats de ces initiatives. En septembre, Yango a présenté son premier Rapport sur la sécurité de Yango Ride (Yango Ride Safety Report). Selon ce rapport, le taux de violations graves du code de la route signalées à lʼéchelle mondiale a diminué de 31 %, passant de 9,83 à 6,76 incidents par million de trajets. Sécurité routière et coopération Les initiatives plus larges de Yango en matière de sécurité comprennent la formation des chauffeurs partenaires, des programmes de distribution de casques et dʼéquipements de protection pour les services de transport à moto, ainsi que des partenariats visant à améliorer la sécurité routière sur les différents marchés où lʼentreprise opère. En collaboration avec les autorités locales et les organisations spécialisées dans la sécurité routière, Yango déploie des programmes de distribution de casques et dʼéquipements de protection destinés aux coursiers partenaires et aux conducteurs de motos partenaires en Asie du Sud, en Afrique et en Amérique latine. Ces programmes comprennent la distribution de centaines de casques dans plusieurs pays, notamment au Pakistan, au Népal, au Sénégal, en Colombie et au Venezuela. À travers son initiative « Safer Journeys to School » (Des trajets plus sûrs vers lʼécole), lancée à Lusaka en partenariat avec le Zambia Road Safety Trust, Yango a combiné lʼaménagement de passages piétons, la mise en place de dispositifs de ralentissement de la circulation et des actions de sensibilisation à la sécurité routière au profit de 32000 élèves répartis dans 20 établissements scolaires. Cette initiative s'est depuis étendue au-delà de la Zambie, notamment au Sénégal, et son lancement est prévu dans dʼautres pays africains. « Nos utilisateurs, nos chauffeurs partenaires et nos coursiers nous font confiance pour prendre leur sécurité au sérieux à chaque trajet. Pour faire progresser notre stratégie, je vois trois priorités complémentaires : utiliser la technologie pour anticiper les risques, renforcer les protocoles qui encadrent nos actions et améliorer concrètement la sécurité sur le terrain, de la formation des conducteurs aux partenariats avec les autorités et les organisations locales. Nous devons développer ces trois axes de manière coordonnée, tirer des enseignements des initiatives qui fonctionnent sur nos différents marchés et les adapter aux réalités locales. Notre responsabilité est dʼêtre à la hauteur de cette confiance chaque jour, à travers nos décisions et nos actions », a déclaré Roman Zemlyansky, Responsable mondial de la sécurité des services de mobilité chez Yango Group. Roman Zemlyansky travaille depuis cinq ans sur les technologies de sécurité dans le secteur du transport avec chauffeur. Il a progressivement évolué du poste de Responsable technique produit (Technical Product Manager) à celui de Responsable des technologies de sécurité (Head of Safety Technologies). Son expérience couvre notamment la vérification de lʼidentité des chauffeurs partenaires et des coursiers, la sécurisation des comptes ainsi que lʼamélioration des indicateurs de sécurité. À propos de Yango Group Yango Group est une entreprise technologique internationale dont le siège est situé aux Émirats arabes unis. Elle contribue à la digitalisation des services urbains essentiels sur les marchés à forte croissance. En associant des technologies internationales à une mise en œuvre locale, lʼentreprise adapte ses services de mobilité, de livraison, de technologie alimentaire (FoodTech), de divertissement et dʼautres services numériques aux besoins de différentes régions et communautés. Ensemble, ces services contribuent à créer un environnement numérique plus connecté et plus pratique pour la vie urbaine, tout en générant de la valeur pour les populations, les entreprises locales et les villes. Yango Group est présent dans plus de 35 pays en Afrique, en Amérique latine, en Europe, au Moyen-Orient, en Asie du Sud et dans dʼautres régions. Pour plus dʼinformations, veuillez contacter : pr@yango.com Cet article YANGO GROUP NOMME UN RESPONSABLE MONDIAL DE LA SÉCURITÉ AFIN DE PILOTER UNE STRATÉGIE UNIFIÉE EN MATIÈRE DE SÉCURITÉ SUR LʼENSEMBLE DE SES MARCHÉS est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: From Arrival to Departure: Improving Ghana’s visitor experience during December in GH 2026
items.description: December in Ghana is more than a season of concerts, parties and celebrations. It is a time when people from different parts of the world come to experience Ghana’s culture, food, music, fashion and hospitality. With the theme “Ghana to the World,” December in GH 2026 presents another opportunity for Ghana to showcase its rich culture and create lasting memories for visitors. However, giving visitors a memorable experience goes beyond organising exciting events. It is also about how they are welcomed, how easily they move around, how safe they feel and the memories they take home. Every stage of their journey matters, from the moment they arrive at the airport until the day they depart. The experience begins at the airport, where visitors form their first impression of Ghana. A smooth arrival process, helpful immigration services and clear information can make visitors feel comfortable and welcomed. During the December in GH stakeholder engagement, the Ghana Immigration Service highlighted the importance of understanding entry requirements, including electronic visa services and visa-free entry arrangements for eligible African nationals. Making these processes clear and accessible can reduce confusion and improve the arrival experience. After arriving, visitors need to move around Ghana with ease. Transportation, accommodation, customer service and access to tourist attractions all contribute to their experience. Whether someone is attending a concert, visiting a heritage site, exploring a local market or enjoying Ghanaian food, they should feel welcomed and respected. Ghana is known for its friendly people, and that warmth should reflect in how visitors are treated by drivers, hotel staff, event organisers and local businesses. Safety is another important part of the visitor experience. People want to enjoy themselves without constantly worrying about their security. At the stakeholder engagement, the Ghana Police Service and National Security emphasised public cooperation through the message, “See Something, Say Something.” Visitors and residents are encouraged to remain alert and report suspicious activities. The emergency contacts shared included 999, 192 for fire emergencies and 18555 for emergency assistance. Event organisers must also provide adequate security, clearly marked fire exits, fire extinguishers and medical support. The National Ambulance Service stressed the importance of standby ambulances, medical posts and trained emergency personnel at major events. These preparations can help visitors enjoy the celebrations with greater confidence. Beyond entertainment, December in GH creates opportunities for hotels, restaurants, transport operators, vendors and tour operators. Visitors spend money on accommodation, food, transportation, shopping and entertainment, supporting businesses across the tourism industry. According to the Ghana Tourism Authority’s 2025 Tourism Report, the December in GH survey recorded average visitor spending of GH₵966.13 on accommodation, GH₵408.31 on food and beverages, and GH₵339.29 on entertainment and recreation. These figures show that the festive season contributes to different areas of the local economy. However, businesses must also provide good customer service, fair treatment and value for money. The Ghana Revenue Authority also reminded businesses and event organisers of their tax responsibilities, including applicable VAT, PAYE and income tax obligations. The importance of improving the visitor experience is also reflected in Ghana’s tourism performance. The 2025 Tourism Report recorded 1,306,962 international arrivals, representing a 1.4% increase from 2024. It also recorded 1,793,797 visits to 55 tourist sites across the country. These figures show the continued growth and importance of tourism to Ghana. More importantly, the December in GH survey revealed that 96% of respondents intended to revisit Ghana, while 90% gave positive ratings to hotels, restaurants and tourist attractions. Although 98% expressed satisfaction with safety and security, only 65% rated their overall experience as excellent or good. These findings are encouraging, but they also show that there is still room for improvement. Ghana must continue to work on transportation, customer service, accommodation and the general organisation of tourism activities to ensure that visitors receive a satisfying experience throughout their stay. As Ghana prepares to welcome the world again, improving the visitor experience must be a shared responsibility. Government institutions, tourism operators, event organisers, businesses and the public all have a role to play. It is not enough to attract people to Ghana; we must also give them good reasons to enjoy their stay, speak positively about the country and recommend it to others. Ultimately, the success of December in GH 2026 should not be measured only by the number of events organised or visitors who arrive. It should also be measured by how visitors feel throughout their stay and the memories they carry home. From arrival to departure, every experience tells a story about Ghana. Let that story be one of warmth, safety, excellent service and unforgettable hospitality. December in GH 2026 should not only give visitors a reason to come, but also a reason to return. items.title: Trump, Poutine, Xi adoptent une « déclaration de paix » après leur sommet inédit
items.description: Donald Trump, Vladimir Poutine et Xi Jinping ont adopté jeudi une « déclaration de paix » affichant leurs ambitions internationales et critique des institutions multilatérales, à l'issue d'un sommet tripartite sans précédent. Au terme de deux jours d'échanges qui ont dominé une rencontre des dirigeants de l'Asie-Pacifique à Shenzhen (sud), les présidents américain, russe et chinois ont discuté pendant environ 1H20 autour d'une imposante table sombre dans une résidence au cadre verdoyant. Ils ont insisté devant les journalistes sur le caractère historique de ce rendez-vous observé avec méfiance par les Européens ou encore Taïwan. Une fois conclu leur entretien organisé après presque cinq ans d'une vaste offensive russe en Ukraine et environ neuf mois de guerre au Moyen-Orient, Chine, Etats-Unis et Russie, des membres permanents du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies, se sont engagés en faveur de la « stabilité stratégique », dans une déclaration diffusée par les médias d'Etat chinois et le Kremlin. Ces pays vont aussi entamer « un dialogue sur la réduction des risques nucléaires et la prévention de la prolifération nucléaire », peut-on lire dans ce texte. Ils y appellent en outre à réformer l'ONU, attaquent la Cour pénale internationale (CPI), qui a émis un mandat d'arrêt visant M. Poutine, et affirment leur volonté d'augmenter les approvisionnements en produits pétroliers, dont les prix se sont envolés ces derniers mois. Etats-Unis et Russie sont des acteurs majeurs du marché et la Chine dispose d'importantes réserves qui lui ont permis de contenir le choc provoqué par la crise. – « Histoire de la diplomatie » – « Nous sommes véritablement en train d'écrire l'Histoire », a déclaré M. Trump au début de cette rencontre qui a laissé craindre des arrangements entre grandes puissances aux dépens d'autres acteurs internationaux comme l'Ukraine et les Européens. Les dirigeants de la Coopération économique Asie-Pacifique (Apec) réunis pour une photo de groupe le 19 novembre 2026 à Shenzhen, en Chine " width="768" height="512" data-src="/resizer/v2/S5VKD3X55FFF3BW6V4SEHXNP7I.png?auth=f7de7396ae782d9e1067448e39a726cad814c6091c7a6c8532a5212a19f451ed" data-srcset="https://www.dhnet.be/resizer/v2/2GIAQ7WQTBA3JCLMSNKRG6PPWA.jpg?auth=1437b13c7b8cc79aad80940504f7c99d6eb0ef11977bd0648fca897e1846f48e&width=768&height=512&quality=85&focal=384%2C256 768w" data-sizes="auto" data-optimumx="1" /> M. Xi a parlé de rendez-vous d'une « portée fondatrice » tandis que M. Poutine a évoqué une nouvelle « page d'Histoire de la diplomatie ». En ouverture des discussions, à l'issue d'un sommet de deux jours des dirigeants de la Coopération économique Asie-Pacifique (Apec), les trois présidents ont évoqué la guerre en Ukraine ou encore la prolifération nucléaire, Donald Trump jugeant que leurs pays se trouvaient dans une « position unique » pour réduire le nombre des armes atomiques dans le monde. Pendant leurs deux jours d'échanges, les trois chefs d'Etat ont multiplié les démonstrations de bonne entente, entre poignées de main, accolades et éloges. – Nouveau Yalta – De gauche à droite le président russe Vladimir Poutine, le président chinois Xi Jinping et le président américain Donald Trump arrivent pour une réunion trilatérale en marge d'un sommet Asie-Pacifique à Shenzen, en Chine " width="768" height="512" data-src="/resizer/v2/S5VKD3X55FFF3BW6V4SEHXNP7I.png?auth=f7de7396ae782d9e1067448e39a726cad814c6091c7a6c8532a5212a19f451ed" data-srcset="https://www.dhnet.be/resizer/v2/Y7NMBW53ZJCMZDKYEPETGZWUVQ.jpg?auth=57ef738bde9c31b25ae9ee3619789406d8fb7cbe2c2487d653d1131660965a48&width=768&height=512&quality=85&focal=384%2C256 768w" data-sizes="auto" data-optimumx="1" /> Cette rencontre sans précédent a suscité des parallèles avec la conférence de Yalta en 1945 à laquelle ont participé les dirigeants américain, britannique et soviétique de l'époque et qui avait jeté les bases de la domination soviétique sur l'Europe de l'Est et tracé les futures lignes de front de la Guerre froide. Pour la Chine, elle constitue une occasion de se poser en acteur incontournable des grandes affaires mondiales. Donald Trump cherche, pour sa part, à faire oublier par des gains diplomatiques la défaite de son camp aux élections de mi-mandat américaines. M. Poutine, quant à lui, peut montrer l'image d'une Russie accueillie en égale par les deux grandes puissances mondiales malgré des sanctions économiques occidentales qu'il a jugées mercredi inefficaces et appartenant « au passé ». Pour la première fois depuis le déclenchement de l'invasion russe de l'Ukraine en février 2022, Vladimir Poutine s'est retrouvé mercredi soir et jeudi matin sur la photo de famille d'un important événement diplomatique en présence de dirigeants occidentaux au-delà des États-Unis (Canada, Australie, Japon). Ses entretiens avec son homologue américain jeudi avant le sommet tripartite ont aussi constitué sa première réunion substantielle avec lui depuis le sommet d'août 2025 en Alaska, qui n'avait pas donné lieu à des avancées majeures. M. Trump n'a pas été avare d'expressions d'amitié avec MM. Poutine et Xi. Il a qualifié d' »ami » le chef de l'Etat russe avec lequel il entretient « une excellente relation depuis de nombreuses années ». Concernant son hôte chinois, « le président Xi et moi avons noué une relation personnelle exceptionnelle », a-t-il assuré. M. Xi était lui-même allé l'accueillir à sa descente d'avion mercredi, ce qu'aucun leader chinois n'avait fait avant lui avec un dirigeant étranger depuis des décennies. – Contrôle de l'IA – Le sommet s'est déroulé à un moment où l'offensive russe en Ukraine approche du cap des cinq ans, sans perspective de règlement rapide. Ce sont les Européens, inquiets du rapprochement entre MM. Trump et Poutine, qui se retrouvent absents et n'ont pas caché leur méfiance vis-à-vis du sommet de Shenzhen. « Ces trois dirigeants ne s'entendent sur rien, et donc il ne va rien sortir de cette réunion-là », a commenté le chef de la diplomatie française Jean-Noël Barrot sur la radio RTL. Autre observatrice attentive, l'île de Taïwan, que la Chine revendique comme faisant partie de son territoire, aura noté les propos attribués par les médias d'Etat à M. Xi et selon lesquels M. Trump devait « continuer à faire » ce qu'il faut pour éviter les « turbulences ». Entre Washington et Pékin, les tensions commerciales persistent en dépit d'une trêve conclue en octobre 2025 mais qui expire en janvier 2027. Chine et Etats-Unis restent engagés dans une intense compétition stratégique et technologique. Les progrès de l'intelligence artificielle (IA) suscitent autant d'attentes que d'inquiétudes internationales. Au cours de la séance plénière des dirigeants de l'Apec en matinée, M. Trump a redit son opposition à « toute forme de réglementation mondialiste » de l'IA. Xi Jinping a réaffirmé que l'IA devait rester « toujours sous contrôle humain » et a souhaité que Chine et Etats-Unis coopèrent à cette fin. AFP L’article Trump, Poutine, Xi adoptent une « déclaration de paix » après leur sommet inédit est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Laâyoune : Youns Bjijou s'informe de l'avancement du futur CHU et du CHR
items.description: Le ministre de la Santé et de la Protection sociale, Youns Bjijou, a effectué, ce jeudi 19 novembre, une visite de terrain à Laâyoune pour inspecter les chantiers du futur Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) ainsi que les travaux de réhabilitation et d’extension du Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) Moulay Hassan Ben El Mehdi. Accompagné du wali de la région Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra, Abdeslam Bekrate, et du directeur général du Groupement sanitaire territorial, Brahim El Ahmadi, le ministre a présidé des réunions techniques visant à lever les contraintes opérationnelles, accélérer la cadence des travaux et fixer les échéances précises de livraison et de mise en service. Premier établissement hospitalo-universitaire des provinces du Sud, le CHU de Laâyoune s’étend sur une superficie globale de plus de 180 000 m², dont 95 000 m² couverts, et offrira une capacité d’accueil de 500 lits au profit de plus de 451 000 habitants de la région et des zones limitrophes. Conçu pour renforcer la formation médicale, la recherche et la prise en charge spécialisée, l'édifice intègre des pôles médico-chirurgicaux complets : prise en charge des cas critiques, urgences, imagerie médicale, cardiologie et maladies vasculaires, néphrologie, ophtalmologie, ORL, pôles mère-enfant et santé mentale, ainsi que des hôpitaux de jour en chirurgie et pédiatrie. Parallèlement, le déplacement ministériel a permis d’évaluer la modernisation du CHR Moulay Hassan Ben El Mehdi, dont la capacité d’accueil est rehaussée de 70 lits supplémentaires afin d’améliorer les conditions d’hospitalisation et la qualité des soins de proximité. S’inscrivant dans le sillage de la réforme du système national de santé et du Nouveau Modèle de Développement des Provinces du Sud, ces deux projets structurants visent à consolider l’équité territoriale en matière d’accès aux soins spécialisés. The post Laâyoune : Youns Bjijou s'informe de l'avancement du futur CHU et du CHR appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘No foreigner will develop Ghana for us’ – Patrick Yaw Boamah demands stronger local business support
items.description: Member of Parliament for Okaikwei Central, Patrick Yaw Boamah, has questioned the government’s commitment to supporting Ghanaian businesses, arguing that the 2027 Budget’s emphasis on private sector growth is not matched by adequate fiscal measures. Contributing to the second day of Parliament’s debate on the budget, Mr Boamah said the government must demonstrate how its economic policies would help local entrepreneurs expand their businesses and create jobs. “The question is, did the budget of 2027 answer the question that a lot of Ghanaian business people are asking with regards to supporting their businesses? Because Mr. Speaker, no foreigner will develop this country for us. We have to develop this country ourselves,” he said. He argued that although the terms “private sector” and “employment” featured prominently in the budget document, the government had not outlined sufficient practical measures to support local businesses. Mr Boamah cited Nigeria’s support for industrialist Aliko Dangote, saying deliberate government backing had helped the businessman expand his operations across Africa, including into Ghana. He also mentioned Ghanaian business figures and investors, including Dr Tettey Assah of Manet, the Adu family of Devtraco and Kevin Otry in the upstream petroleum sector, as examples of local entrepreneurs whose businesses could benefit from targeted state support. “So it’s a step that we must be serious about. We must be deliberate about it and we must put our money where the fiscal incentives and the waivers that requires of supporting the business community of this country,” he added. He said stronger support for businesses was important to expanding employment opportunities, particularly for young people. MP questions directive on SOE board allowances Mr Boamah also raised concerns about a Ministry of Finance directive asking more than 164 state-owned enterprises and statutory institutions to stop paying monthly sitting allowances to board members. He told Parliament that a letter dated October 12, 2026, and signed by a Deputy Finance Minister on behalf of the Minister had been sent to the affected institutions. “These are state companies, these are statutory institutions that require regular board meetings to help grow those companies. But this is a directive by the Minister of Finance asking for board allowance not to be paid. And this is a very serious matter that must be looked into by the House,” he said. He argued that the directive could affect the governance of state enterprises and called for Parliament to examine the matter. Boamah demands explanation for GH¢100m judgment debt allocation The Okaikwei Central MP further asked the Finance Minister to explain a GH¢100 million allocation for judgment debt payments in the 2027 Budget, directing attention to page 195, Appendix 4A. He said the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) was facing a judgment debt claim exceeding GH¢680 million involving Safari Tech. “As I speak to you, GRA is saddled with a judgment debt of over 680 million Ghana Cedis from Safari Tech,” he stated. Mr Boamah also criticised a proposed amendment to the State Proceedings Act, which he said could restrict creditors from attaching funds in the Contingency Fund or Consolidated Fund when seeking to enforce judgments against the state. He argued that government institutions must honour contractual obligations to avoid the accumulation of judgment debts. “The government must respect the contracts that they enter into. State institutions must respect contracts to prevent the occurrence of judgment debts,” he said. He also referred to outstanding debt issues involving Ghana Water Company and Abengoa, as well as Tullow Oil Ghana, as examples of liabilities requiring attention. MP raises oversight concerns over GH¢30bn New Economy fund Mr Boamah also urged Parliament to exercise close oversight over the proposed GH¢30 billion allocation for the government’s New Economy agenda. Referring to page 189 of the budget, he said the amount was captured as capital expenditure without being allocated to specific ministries. “There’s no ministry called New Economy,” he said, contrasting the arrangement with the previous budget, which he said allocated funding directly to ministries. He mentioned proposed allocations of GH¢3 billion for agriculture, GH¢2.2 billion for mining and GH¢1 billion for telecommunications, but questioned why the funds were not assigned directly to the relevant ministries. Mr Boamah warned that keeping the allocation under the Finance Ministry could weaken Parliament’s ability to monitor how the money was distributed and used. “We as a House must have the power or the oversight to check whether those monies were sent to the ministries and whether they were properly utilized,” he said. He cautioned Parliament against giving the Finance Minister excessive control over the funds over the next four years, arguing that allocations intended for agriculture and other sectors should be channelled through the relevant ministries. His comments add to parliamentary scrutiny of the proposed budget, particularly its approach to private sector development, public liabilities and the management of major spending programmes.

items.title: Buhari told me he would always do what was right, regardless of who was involved — BUA chairman
items.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor The Chairman of BUA Group, Alhaji Abdul Samad Rabiu, has recounted how former President Muhammadu Buhari stood by him during a difficult period in his business, insisting that he would always do what was right, irrespective of those involved. Rabiu said Buhari’s commitment to justice and fairness helped save his business when he faced challenges with some government agencies. He disclosed this in a goodwill message delivered on his behalf by Senator Lawal Shuaibu at the launch of Buhari: The Authorised Biography. The message was shared by Buhari’s former Senior Special Assistant on Media and Publicity, Garba Shehu, on his X handle on Thursday. Describing Buhari as a father, mentor, trusted friend and pillar of strength to him and his family, Rabiu said the former President stood by him during some of the most difficult moments of his life and business. He recalled facing enormous challenges with certain government agencies, which he said threatened the survival of his business and years of investment. According to him, Buhari stood firmly on the side of justice despite strong resistance and pressure from those who wanted him to act otherwise. “I remember vividly when he assured me that he would always do what was right, regardless of who was involved or how powerful they might be. I was moved to tears by those words and by his genuine concern for me,” he said. Rabiu said Buhari’s determination to uphold justice ultimately saved his business, adding that he would remain eternally grateful for the former President’s intervention. He described the former President as a man of uncommon integrity, humility and simplicity, who devoted much of his life to the service of Nigeria. “To the nation, he was a President and a statesman. To me and my family, he was much more. He was a father figure, a cherished family friend and a source of wisdom, encouragement and comfort,” he said. The BUA chairman, who said he was unable to attend the event because of a previously scheduled engagement in London, expressed regret over his absence. He also announced a pledge of N500 million towards the purchase of 1,000 copies of the biography in honour of Buhari. Rabiu said he had authorised Shuaibu to announce the donation on his behalf, describing the book as an important work that would help preserve the former President’s life, service and legacy for generations. He prayed for Allah’s forgiveness for Buhari’s shortcomings, reward for his good deeds and a place for him in Jannatul Firdaus, while also expressing condolences to his family and loved ones. items.title: Siguiri : le procureur général hausse le ton et ordonne la traque des orpailleurs clandestins
items.description: La lutte contre l’orpaillage clandestin et la dégradation de l’environnement se durcit dans le ressort de la Cour d’appel de Kankan. En mission à Siguiri, le procureur général près ladite cour a instruit le procureur de la République près le tribunal de première instance de Siguiri, ainsi que les autres parquets relevant de son ressort, de veiller à l’application stricte des mesures interdisant l’exploitation anarchique de l’or. Face à l’ampleur des dégâts environnementaux causés par cette activité dans la région de Siguiri, le parquet général entend renforcer la réponse judiciaire. À cet effet, le procureur général a rappelé que les mesures administratives prises pour interdire l’orpaillage clandestin doivent être rigoureusement appliquées, sans aucune complaisance. « J’instruis le procureur de la République près le tribunal de première instance de Siguiri de veiller à l’application stricte, sans délai, de cette mesure interdisant l’orpaillage illégal dans ce ressort territorial », a-t-il déclaré. Ces instructions ne concernent pas uniquement Siguiri. Elles s’étendent également aux parquets de Kouroussa, Mandiana, Kankan, Kérouané, N’Zérékoré et Lola, dans le cadre d’une action judiciaire coordonnée à l’échelle du ressort de la Cour d’appel de Kankan. Le procureur général a, par ailleurs, salué l’engagement du procureur spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), dont le parquet dispose de compétences en matière de poursuites liées aux infractions environnementales. Il l’a encouragé à poursuivre les procédures engagées contre les personnes mises en cause dans les affaires de dégradation de l’environnement liées à l’exploitation illégale de l’or. À travers ces instructions, le parquet général affiche sa volonté de renforcer la répression de l’orpaillage clandestin et de garantir l’application effective des décisions administratives et des dispositions pénales en vigueur. Une fermeté judiciaire qui intervient dans un contexte de préoccupations croissantes face à la dégradation de l’environnement dans la région de Siguiri.

items.title: Prosecutor confident Jirapa Dubai murder conviction will survive Supreme Court challenge
items.description: Principal State Attorney Saeed Abdul Shakur says the prosecution is confident that Elisha Mahama Akpanichie’s conviction for the murder of businessman Eric Johnson will stand if he challenges the Court of Appeal’s decision at the Supreme Court. The Court of Appeal on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, dismissed Mahama’s appeal against his conviction, upholding the life sentence imposed by the Wa High Court. Mr Abdul Shakur said the prosecution remained convinced that the evidence presented during the trial sufficiently established Mahama’s involvement in the murder. He identified telephone records and footprint evidence as key elements of the prosecution’s case. “The evidence we put before the court, especially the phone records and the footprints, put Elisha Mahama right in the bedroom of the deceased,” he said. He said the Court of Appeal’s decision affirmed the prosecution’s position and left the original judgment unchanged. “The court essentially agreed with what we did in the court and then dismissed the appeal,” he said. “The judgment of the Wa High Court was not disturbed. Elisha Mahama is still serving a lifetime in jail.” Mahama had challenged aspects of his trial, including the directions given to the jury by the trial judge and the qualifications of a fingerprint examiner whose evidence was presented by the prosecution. Mr Abdul Shakur maintained that the prosecution had properly established its case and was prepared to defend the conviction if Mahama pursued a further appeal. “If he decides to challenge the decision in the Supreme Court, we will be there or thereabouts to also make our case because we believe strongly that nothing untoward was done,” he said. The Principal State Attorney said the Court of Appeal’s ruling would offer some satisfaction to Johnson’s family, although it could not undo their loss. He described Johnson as an industrious businessman whose contribution to the Upper West Region would be difficult to replace. “He has left a huge hole in the Upper West Region,” he said. Johnson, 60, was the founder and Chief Executive Officer of Royal Cosy Hills Hotel and Safari Resort, popularly known as Jirapa Dubai. Two other people initially charged in connection with the murder — a female hotel employee and a security officer — were acquitted and discharged. Mahama was the only person convicted in the case.

items.title: 'Giving students hope for a better future': Schools in Pakistan, UK, Nigeria among winners in global prizes
items.description: Schools in Britain, Nigeria, Brazil, Pakistan and South Korea were named winners of the World’s Best School Prizes on Thursday for work including supporting student well-being, helping underserved communities and coordinating support for children with complex learning needs. The winners are invited to January’s World Schools Summit in London to present their approaches to policymakers and education figures, organiser T4 Education, a global network for educators, said. The annual prize comes weeks after high school pupils in France blockaded schools demanding renovation of their buildings, more teachers and university reforms, a movement that broadened into protests over the cost of living, drawing in trade unionists and activists and at times turning violent. “Young people are simply worried about their future,” T4 Education and prizes founder Vikas Pota told Reuters . “What our schools are doing … especially the winning schools … (is that) they’re all giving students hope for a better future … They’re responding to what the communities want.” Swiss Cottage School, Development and Research Centre, a London state primary and secondary special school, won the Community Collaboration prize for bringing together different services to support pupils with complex learning needs, many from lower-income backgrounds. The school links education, community participation, therapy, healthcare and employability support, connecting classroom learning to the wider world. Slum2School Green Academy in Epe, Nigeria, won the Environmental Action prize. The charity-run kindergarten and primary school, which serves about 250 children from river communities, was recognised for its environmentally designed buildings and a model combining practical, project and play-based learning. The school runs on solar power and is built from natural materials such as wood and bamboo. Pupils learn about sustainable practices including water conservation, waste management and renewable energy. Public primary school Escola Municipal GET IV Centenario won the Overcoming Adversity prize for its hands-on learning model focused on creativity, emotional development and student leadership, serving 261 students. Based in Rio de Janeiro’s Complexo da Mar favela community, the school was closed for 37 days in 2024 because of local violence. It runs a “Dream Factory” program in which pupils use technology to address local problems. The Supporting Healthy Lives award went to TNS Beaconhouse, an independent school in Lahore with more than 1,100 students across kindergarten, primary and secondary levels, for its approach to supporting neurodivergent learners. Independent secondary school G-School in Seoul won the Innovation prize. Each of its nearly 70 students takes on a long-term social problem-solving project; one team persuaded 27 local businesses to install wheelchair ramps to improve accessibility. A separate prize decided by public vote, the Community Choice award, went to Darussafaka Egitim Kurumlari, a full-scholarship boarding school in Istanbul, for a two-track model that includes remote learning for children affected by earthquakes.

items.title: 2027: Soludo urges Anambra voters to support APC, warns against political isolation
items.description: Sekinat Osundiji Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has urged residents of the state to reconsider their voting pattern ahead of the 2027 presidential election, warning that political isolation could further weaken the South-East’s influence in national affairs. Soludo made the appeal on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, attended by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC National Chairman and other party leaders and governors. The governor described the rally as unique, noting that Anambra recorded only 5,111 votes, representing 0.8 per cent of the total votes cast for the APC during the 2023 presidential election. He challenged residents to improve on the state’s previous performance in the 2027 election, pointing to the need for a different voting outcome. Soludo, who said he had held town hall meetings across the state in recent weeks, appealed to residents to approach political discussions with reason rather than confrontation. He acknowledged the grievances and frustrations among some residents over national political developments but maintained that the campaign should provide an opportunity for constructive engagement about Nigeria and the interests of the Igbo people. The governor questioned whether the South-East could afford further political isolation, particularly after the economic losses associated with the Monday sit-at-home order in the region. He said the region needed to consider the consequences of political isolation and explore ways of building alliances with other parts of the country. “Can a people who have lost one full year of work in five years afford further political isolation?” Soludo asked. Soludo also questioned what political leverage the Igbo people could exercise in a democracy beyond their votes and alliances with other regions. He argued that the region’s participation in national political alliances was important to its ability to influence decisions and advance its interests. “What do we have as leverage in a democracy other than our votes and alliances with the rest of the country?” he asked. The governor also cautioned against dismissing the consequences of repeated electoral losses, insisting that the region must consider the political implications of its voting decisions. “Losing has consequences,” he said. Soludo advocated a political approach centred on building bridges across the country, saying greater engagement with other regions would create opportunities for the South-East. He said the Igbo people needed a peaceful and prosperous Nigeria where they could live, work and thrive regardless of their location. He added that the region could not afford to isolate itself from other parts of the country, particularly in the face of ethnic and religious intolerance. “We cannot afford to lock ourselves up in one corner and breed lamentations. We need to get out and engage with Nigeria,” he said. The governor maintained that building bridges and participating actively in national politics remained central to securing the political and economic interests of the Igbo people. The post 2027: Soludo urges Anambra voters to support APC, warns against political isolation appeared first on Vanguard News .

Airport Police locate family of deceased man
items.description: The Airport Police Command, Lagos, has established contact with the family of a deceased man, Abraham Safety Osakpolor, following a public appeal for assistance in locating his relatives. The command disclosed this in a statement posted on its X handle on Thursday, expressing appreciation to members of the public and media organisations who helped circulate its earlier appeal. The statement, signed by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Mohammed Adeola, said the command successfully established contact with Osakpolor’s family after seeking public assistance in identifying his relatives and friends. It thanked individuals, media organisations and other members of the public who shared and reposted the earlier announcement, noting that their collective efforts made the development possible. The Commissioner of Police, Airport Police Command, CP Olufunke Ogunbode, reiterated the importance of public cooperation in effective policing. Ogunbode said effective policing thrived on mutual trust, cooperation and shared responsibility, while reaffirming the command’s commitment to maintaining a cordial and productive relationship with the public. The command had earlier issued an appeal seeking information that could help identify and locate the family and friends of the deceased. items.title: Gazoduc TSGP : une délégation algérienne au Niger pour finaliser cinq étapes clés
items.description: Alger et Niamey mettent les bouchées doubles pour lancer au plus vite la partie nigérienne du gazoduc transsaharien TSGP reliant le Nigeria à l’Europe via le Niger et l'Algérie. Les deux pays doivent finaliser cinq étapes clés avant le lancement des travaux. Une délégation technique algérienne se trouve au Niger pour mettre au point avec ses vis-à-vis nigériens les préparatifs du lancement des travaux dans ce pays. Gazoduc TSGP : une délégation technique algérienne au Niger Le TSGP est un important projet transfrontalier devant acheminer le gaz du Nigeria en Europe via les territoires nigérien et algérien. Sa capacité est d’environ 30 milliards de mètres cubes par an, en utilisant les gazoducs déjà existants en Algérie et au Nigeria. Il reste à réaliser les parties manquantes dans ces deux pays et toute la section qui traversera le Niger. Les travaux sur le tronçon algérien ont été lancés en juin dernier et les préparatifs vont bon train pour en faire de même sur le territoire nigérien. Une délégation du secteur énergétique algérien se trouve en mission de travail dans ce pays voisin du 17 au 20 novembre, annonce Sonatrach dans un communiqué. Elle est composée de cadres du ministère des Hydrocarbures, de l’Activité transport par canalisation de Sonatrach et de l’Entreprise nationale de canalisation (ENAC), filiale du géant pétrolier et gazier algérien. La délégation algérienne a été reçue mardi 17 novembre par le secrétaire général du ministère nigérien du Pétrole, Abdoulkarim Mohamed Ali. Confirmation du tracé du gazoduc modifié par le Niger La rencontre entre dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du processus de réalisation du TSGP dans sa partie nigérienne et s’inscrit dans le sillage des travaux de construction du tronçon algérien, déjà engagés par Sonatrach, “marquant une avancée importante dans la réalisation de cette infrastructure énergétique régionale”, explique Sonatrach. Elle s’inscrit également dans le cadre de “l’engagement de la partie nigérienne à accélérer les préparatifs liés au gazoduc”, ajoute le communiqué. À propos de la teneur des discussions, Sonatrach a précisé qu’elles ont porté notamment sur “l’accélération des études techniques relatives au tracé du gazoduc sur le territoire nigérien ainsi que le recueil de toutes les informations en relation avec les phases du projet”, “la confirmation du tracé modifié par le Niger et l’évaluation de son impact”, et “l’identification des prestations et des études à prévoir dans le scope of work”. ENAC, filiale de Sonatrach, crée une succursale au Niger Il a été également question de la possibilité de “la participation des entreprises locales nigériennes aux prestations et aux études réglementaires, conformément aux engagements déjà annoncés”, de même qu'ont été évoquées “les modalités de création par ENAC, chargée de la réalisation des études de tracés, d’une succursale au Niger.” Il s'agit de la deuxième réunion de coordination technique entre les deux parties. Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre de la poursuite des engagements de l’Algérie “à œuvrer à consolider ses partenariats stratégiques avec les pays africains frères et à renforcer la présence du groupe Sonatrach sur la scène énergétique continentale et internationale”, conclut le communiqué de Sonatrach. L’article Gazoduc TSGP : une délégation algérienne au Niger pour finaliser cinq étapes clés est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Court of Appeal upholds life sentence for Jirapa Dubai CEO’s killer
items.description: The Court of Appeal has dismissed an appeal by Elisha Mahama Akpanichie against his conviction for the murder of Eric Johnson, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Royal Cosy Hills Hotel and Safari Resort, popularly known as Jirapa Dubai. The court delivered its decision on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, affirming the life sentence imposed on Mahama by the Wa High Court on October 15, 2025. Mahama, a former Human Resource Manager of the hotel, had challenged the conviction, arguing that the trial judge made errors in the directions given to the jury. He also questioned the qualifications and expertise of a fingerprint examiner whose testimony formed part of the prosecution’s evidence. The prosecution had relied on forensic evidence, including fingerprints and footprints, as well as telephone records, to establish its case against him. However, the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal, leaving both the conviction and life sentence unchanged. Two other people who were initially charged alongside Mahama — a female hotel employee and a security officer — were acquitted and discharged after the court found insufficient evidence against them. Mahama was the only person convicted in connection with the murder. The decision means he remains subject to the life sentence imposed by the Wa High Court, although he may pursue a further appeal before the Supreme Court.

items.title: Singandé : ces échelles géantes qui défient la hauteur et rapprochent les habitants à Lélouma
items.description: Singandé! C’est le chemin obligé des citoyens du district de Kenté dans la sous-préfecture de Korbé pour rallier le centre-ville de Lélouma. Ces gigantesques échelles accrochées sur la montagne culminent à plusieurs dizaines de mètres de hauteur. Tenez! Ces échelles de Singandé semblent défier le vide, la hauteur. Au premier coup d’œil, elles donnent la trouille, le vertige. Cependant, pour les habitants, qui les utilisent quotidiennement, ce n’est ni un décor, encore moins un site touristique: c’est un passage vital pour rallier la commune urbaine et vice-versa. Un chemin quotidien suspendu entre la montagne et le vide. “ C’est le chemin le plus rapide pour partir à Lélouma centre pour nous qui vivons en bas de la montagne. Faute de quoi nous allons faire un détour de plusieurs dizaines de kilomètres. (…) Ces échelles sont essentielles pour nous. C’est le chemin le plus court et le plus emprunté des habitants”, précise un jeune homme sur les marches des échelles. Ici, il suffit juste de voir l’ouvrage pour comprendre qu’on a à faire à un passage qui sort de l’ordinaire. L’endroit peut impressionner même les personnes les plus téméraires. Ces longues échelles métalliques solidement accrochées à la paroi rocheuse conjuguent avec un relief montagneux qui s’élève sur plusieurs dizaines de mètres de hauteur. Leur inclinaison, le vide qui les entoure et la hauteur sont fascinants. Pour certains visiteurs qui découvrent le lieu, l’idée même de s’y engager peut provoquer une certaine appréhension. Pour les populations qui empruntent régulièrement ces échelles, le chemin vers la ville commence par une véritable ascension.

items.title: President, PM agree on resolving 'all matters' through dialogue amid rising political temperatures
items.description: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have decided that all matters will be resolved through dialogue, the Presidency said on Thursday after the two leaders met in Islamabad. The meeting follows recent hard-hitting remarks by President Zardari’s son, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, who questioned past decisions and actions taken by the ruling coalition — steered by PML-N and supported by PPP. In a statement, the Presidency said the “current situation” was discussed in Thursday’s meeting. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, whom Bilawal made pointed remarks about, was also present at the huddle. The “current political situation was reviewed in detail”, while the Middle East conflict also came under discussion. It was decided that the leadership will “sit down together on all matters and resolve them through consultation”, the Presidency said. “The previous constitutional amendments were passed through mutual consultation among all allied parties,” the statement from President Zardari’s office said. The recent friction between coalition partners PML-N and PPP comes amid a debate over the creation of new administrative units, which was sparked by Naqvi in July when he called for a “reset” in governance. The PPP has consistently opposed carving out new provinces in Sindh, which it rules. The party has consistently invoked a unanimous resolution passed by the Sindh Assembly opposing the province’s division, although President Zardari has not commented on the matter publicly. Bilawal’s remarks on Tuesday drew a strong reaction from leaders of the PML-N, as well as the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) — another coalition ally. Despite months having passed since the debate began, Bilawal claimed that no one from the government had brought up the matter with him or President Zardari, even though some federal ministers have voiced their support for more provinces. His remarks followed the Nov 14 meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz. According to official sources, the two reached an understanding on sticking to the constitutional process for any new provinces. Speaking at a ‘Meet the Press’ event in Karachi, the Bhutto scion expressed the fear that any “forced” attempt to carve up Sindh into new provinces would lead to bloodshed. He also voiced his strong opposition to a referendum on creating new provinces — as initially suggested by Naqvi and endorsed by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar in response to Bilawal’s speech. Bilawal even questioned whether the judiciary had the public’s confidence, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, which he had strongly advocated for at the time of its passage just a year ago. He said that the 27th Amendment was passed with a “ brute majority ” rather than a mutual consensus. However, in a later interview, Bilawal clarified that he was not “disowning” the amendment, but rather advocating for greater consensus on such key legislation. As he called for a “political and democratic reset” to meet the growing economic challenges, the PPP chairman suggested some steps the government could take to restore the opposition’s confidence so the Parliament could function properly.
