items.title: Declare state of emergency in galamsey hotspots – Catholic Bishops to Mahama
items.description: The Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference (GCBC) has called on President John Dramani Mahama to declare a targeted state of emergency in areas severely affected by illegal mining, popularly known as Galamsey. The Bishops say government interventions have so far failed to produce the desired results, warning that illegal mining continues to threaten water bodies, forest reserves, agricultural lands and public health. They have also drawn attention to growing indiscipline in schools, drug trafficking and abuse, and conflicts in some parts of the country. In a communiqué issued at the end of their annual Plenary Assembly in Jamasi in the Ashanti Region, the Conference, led by its President, Most Rev. Matthew Kwasi Gyamfi, said stronger measures are needed to confront these vices. “Considering that the interventions put in place by the government of President Mahama are so far not producing the desired, promised and expected end of the menace of galamsey, we believe that it is NOW time to declare a targeted state of emergency in the locations most affected by illegal and irresponsible mining,” he stated. The Bishops are also calling for stronger collaboration among regulatory institutions, security agencies, traditional authorities, religious leaders and citizens to confront illegal mining networks, ensure accountability and provide sustainable livelihood alternatives for affected communities. On education, Most Rev. Matthew Kwasi Gyamfi and the Bishops expressed concern over growing indiscipline in some schools, including mission institutions, citing reports of violence, examination malpractice, vandalism and alleged sexual abuse of minors by adults entrusted with their care. They called on the Ministry of Education, the Ghana Education Service, school authorities and the Police to investigate the allegations and ensure that the law takes its course. The Conference further urged a renewed government-missions partnership in managing mission schools, stressing that education must produce not only academically competent individuals but also responsible and morally grounded citizens. The Bishops also raised concerns about drug trafficking and substance abuse, describing the trend as a threat to public health, family stability, youth development and national security. They are urging relevant institutions to intensify intelligence-led enforcement, border controls, public education and rehabilitation services to address the problem. On national security, the Conference expressed concern over persistent communal conflicts in Bawku and Kalba-Gbinyiri, calling on all parties to renounce violence and embrace dialogue and reconciliation. It also urged the full and timely implementation of recommendations in the relevant report on the Kalba-Gbinyiri conflict, noting that lasting peace requires justice, mutual recognition and the protection of affected communities. Meanwhile, the Bishops have called for the responsible integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Ghanaian society, acknowledging its potential to advance human development but cautioning against threats to human dignity, privacy, truth and social cohesion. They said technological advancement must remain at the service of humanity and the common good, urging the Church to strengthen education, research and ethical reflection on the use of AI. The Conference also warned against misinformation, disinformation and the deliberate manipulation of digital platforms, while emphasising the need to protect personal data. The communiqué followed the Bishops’ annual Plenary Assembly held from November 3 to 14, 2026, at the Divine Providence Pastoral Centre in Jamasi. It was held under the theme, “Communion, Participation and Mission: Preparing the Catholic Church in Ghana for Her 150th Anniversary in 2030.” As part of preparations towards the milestone, the Bishops announced a three-year spiritual focus, dedicating 2027 to Jesus Christ, the Son of God; 2028 to the Holy Spirit; and 2029 to God the Father, ahead of the climax of the celebrations in 2030. The Catholic Church in Ghana traces its beginnings to 1880.

items.description: La diversification du tissu industriel gabonais pourrait franchir un nouveau palier avec la perspective d’implantation d’une plateforme industrielle et logistique à Kango, dans la province de l’Estuaire. Autour de cette ambition, le ministre du Commerce, de l’Industrie et de la Transformation, Emmanuel Eyeghe Nze, a échangé, le 19 novembre, avec une délégation du groupe Arise, conduite par son directeur pays, Igor Simard, accompagné de Gaurav Aggarwal, directeur général de Gabon special economic zone (GSEZ). Le ministre du Commerce, de l’Industrie et de la Transformation, Emmanuel Eyeghe Nze, et la délégation du groupe Arise, le 19 novembre 2026, à Libreville. © D.R. Le Gabon envisage de doter Kango, dans la province de l’Estuaire, d’une nouvelle zone industrielle spéciale. Le ministre du Commerce, de l’Industrie et de la Transformation, Emmanuel Eyeghe Nze, a reçu ce jeudi 19 novembre une délégation du groupe Arise, conduite par son directeur pays, Igor Simard, accompagnée du directeur général de GSEZ – Gabon Special Economic Zone, Gaurav Aggarwal, afin d’examiner les perspectives de ce projet structurant. Les discussions ont porté sur les perspectives de partenariat et les conditions d’accompagnement de ce projet structurant. Fort de son expérience dans l’aménagement de la zone d’investissement spéciale de Nkok, GSEZ a exprimé son intérêt pour cette nouvelle orientation industrielle. « Cette rencontre a permis d’examiner les perspectives de partenariat autour de ce projet structurant », a indiqué le compte rendu des échanges. Renforcer le tissu industriel national À travers cette initiative, les autorités entendent étendre le modèle des zones industrielles spéciales, renforcer les capacités productives nationales et stimuler la transformation locale. Une ambition qui vise notamment, selon des sources du ministère du Commerce, à « renforcer le tissu industriel national d’accélérer la transformation locale des ressources naturelles et de favoriser la création d’emplois ». Présenté le 13 novembre dernier au ministre du Logement, Mays Mouissi, le projet de Kango prévoit notamment des infrastructures de stockage du manganèse, le développement de la filière bois et une unité de production de biocharbon à partir des résidus forestiers. Sa concrétisation reste néanmoins subordonnée à la sécurisation foncière du site. Aucun montant d’investissement, calendrier d’exécution ni objectif d’emploi n’a, à ce stade, été communiqué. L’article Industrie : le Gabon veut étendre le modèle de Nkok à Kango est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: Twifo Hemang residents demand ECG action over high electricity bills
items.description: Residents of Twifo Hemang in the Central Region have called on the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) to address concerns over high electricity bills, discrepancies in meter details and difficulties accessing customer support. They say the challenges have left some consumers struggling to settle their bills and are demanding improved customer service and urgent intervention from the power distributor. The Queen Mother of Twifo Hemang, Nana Adwoa Obeng Aso II, said one of her major concerns was receiving electricity bills bearing meter numbers that did not correspond with the meter installed at her premises. She welcomed a sensitisation forum organised by ECG, describing it as an opportunity for residents to seek clarification and gain a better understanding of the company’s billing processes. Another resident, Yaw Frimpong, said the existing ECG office at Twifo Praso was inadequate to serve consumers in Twifo Hemang and surrounding communities. He called for the establishment of a customer service office in Twifo Hemang to improve access to ECG services and make it easier for residents to resolve billing complaints. “We have realised their Twifo Praso office cannot cater to all of us. So, we need an office in Twifo Hemang to address our problems,” he said. ECG responds Responding to the concerns, ECG’s Central Regional Public Relations Officer, Esther Anjola, announced plans to intensify community-level education and take the company’s services closer to consumers. She said the company would deploy franchise officers to various communities to take meter readings, identify discrepancies and facilitate corrections to affected bills. “From next week, we are going to organise community-by-community education, where we will take our systems to their doorsteps. We will be sending our franchise officers to pick the readings so we can correct the bills for them,” she said. Ms Anjola added that billing concerns that could be resolved would be addressed within the respective communities, reducing the need for residents to travel to ECG offices for assistance. The exercise is expected to allow consumers to have their meter readings verified and billing discrepancies addressed while improving access to the company’s services.

items.title: Erastus Asare Donkor laments as court acquits four suspects who attacked him during galamsey exposé
items.description: Investigative journalist Erastus Asare Donkor has expressed disappointment following the acquittal and discharge of four people accused in connection with an alleged attack on him and his colleagues while they were covering illegal mining activities in the Asenanyo Forest Reserve in the Ashanti Region. The journalist, in a lengthy social media post on Thursday, November 19, 2026, described the outcome as a possible miscarriage of justice, recounting the ordeal he and his team allegedly suffered during the assignment in late 2024. According to him, the team was gathering evidence on the destruction of a reclaimed portion of the forest reserve when they were confronted by a group of heavily built men armed with pump-action and other rifles. He alleged that the men abducted them and drove them to an area near Manso Nkran, where they were subjected to severe beatings. Mr Asare Donkor said he was slapped repeatedly, while his colleagues, identified as Eddie, Majid and Nicholas, later required hospital checks for injuries involving their ears, eyes and noses. He further alleged that the attackers took some of their working equipment and personal belongings, including drone batteries, his jacket containing identification cards and a JBL headset. Court case ends in acquittal The journalist said the team subsequently reported the incident to the Manso Adubia Police, who initially accompanied them to the scene. However, he alleged that despite encountering some of the men they identified as their attackers, the police failed to make any arrests. He also recounted a subsequent visit involving officers from the Bekwai Police, which he said did not result in any arrests. According to him, three suspects were eventually presented by the Manso Adubia Police about a week later, with officers indicating that the men had handed themselves in. The case proceeded to the Bekwai Circuit Court, where he said the prosecution was committed to securing justice but accused the investigator of failing to properly gather and document crucial evidence. He specifically alleged that the investigator failed to include evidence from the field in the case docket and did not investigate injuries sustained by their driver. The matter took another turn on November 17, 2026, when the four accused persons were acquitted and discharged by the Obuasi High Court after their appeal on a submission of no case to answer was successful, according to a message from the prosecutor shared by the journalist. The prosecutor’s message further indicated that the case was struck out at the circuit court on November 19. Reacting to the development, Mr Asare Donkor said he was disappointed by the outcome after more than a year of court proceedings. Journalist recounts death threats Beyond the court case, the investigative journalist disclosed that he has received repeated threats to his life over his environmental reporting, particularly his coverage of illegal mining activities. He alleged that on one occasion, a man went to his child’s school and took photographs of the child while he was outside the country. He also recounted an incident in which another person was allegedly stabbed after being mistaken for his relative, claiming that the attackers had threatened to send him the person’s head as a warning. Mr Asare Donkor said he had reported the threats to the Ghana Police Service but expressed frustration that, in his view, little conclusive action had followed. He also recalled being subjected to curses by members of a community over his reporting on alleged illegal mining activities in Manso Tontokrom. Despite the threats and challenges, the journalist insisted that financial reward was not his motivation, maintaining that his environmental reporting had helped draw attention to the destruction of several forest reserves. He listed Apamprama, Tano Nimri, Tano Anwia, Boin River and Jimira among the forest reserves he believes his work has helped protect from further destruction. In an emotional conclusion to his statement, Mr Asare Donkor said he was leaving those he accused of attacking him to face divine judgment. He maintained that his commitment to environmental journalism would not be shaken by threats, intimidation or public criticism.

El Jadida : une vidéo de maltraitance contre mineurs déclenche une double enquête
items.description: La diffusion d’une vidéo montrant des scènes présumées de violences physiques au sein de Dar Talib d’El Jadida a déclenché une double enquête, judiciaire et administrative. Les images, largement relayées sur les réseaux sociaux, montrent des bénéficiaires de cet établissement d’hébergement pour élèves victimes d’agressions physiques présumées. Les autorités sécuritaires et gouvernementales ont engagé des investigations pour établir les faits et déterminer les éventuelles responsabilités. Mercredi 18 novembre, les services de la sûreté régionale d’El Jadida ont ouvert une enquête judiciaire sous la supervision du parquet compétent. Les investigations doivent notamment permettre de vérifier l’authenticité de la vidéo diffusée et de reconstituer les circonstances dans lesquelles les faits se seraient produits. Selon une source sécuritaire, les services de veille informatique de la Direction générale de la sûreté nationale (DGSN) ont détecté les images, qui documenteraient une agression physique présumée au sein d’un établissement accueillant des élèves scolarisés. Leur contenu a été soumis aux investigations judiciaires nécessaires. Les recherches se poursuivent sous la supervision du parquet afin de déterminer les circonstances et les éléments ayant entouré l’incident. Les enquêteurs cherchent également à établir les motivations de la personne ayant filmé la séquence et décidé de la diffuser sur les réseaux sociaux. En parallèle, le ministère de la Famille, du Développement social et de l’Égalité a annoncé l’ouverture d’une enquête administrative à la suite des informations faisant état de violences contre des bénéficiaires de Dar Talib d’El Jadida. Le département affirme suivre l’affaire avec une attention particulière et condamne fermement toute pratique portant atteinte à la dignité ou à l’intégrité physique et psychologique des pensionnaires des établissements de protection sociale. Le ministère rappelle que ces structures ont vocation à garantir un environnement sûr, assurant la protection, la prise en charge ainsi que l’accompagnement éducatif et social de leurs bénéficiaires. Elles sont tenues de respecter leurs droits et de préserver leur dignité, sans tolérer aucune forme de violence, d’humiliation ou de mauvais traitement. L'enquête administrative engagée doit permettre de vérifier la véracité des faits rapportés, d'en cerner les circonstances et d'identifier les responsabilités éventuelles. Le ministère indique que les conclusions des investigations détermineront les mesures administratives et judiciaires à prendre, dans le respect des dispositions légales en vigueur. The post El Jadida : une vidéo de maltraitance contre mineurs déclenche une double enquête appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: British hacker who stole $11m through text message scheme jailed for six years in US
items.description: A British hacker has been sentenced to six years in a federal prison in the US for conspiring to hack into at least a dozen companies via text message phishing, and stealing more than $11.6m (£8.8m) in cryptocurrency from individual victims. Tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, started hacking as a teenager and was part of the collective of young hackers known as Scattered Spider, which has been blamed for a string of high profile cyber-crimes. US prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims and showed the growing threat posed by online crime groups. The sentence brings to an end a years-long international investigation involving authorities in the UK, US, Spain and Canada. Buchanan admitted taking part in a hacking campaign that began in 2021, when he was 19. Working from his parents’ home, he and other English-speaking hackers in the US and UK targeted employees at major technology and telecommunications companies. It made them $8m in less than two years, according to US prosecutors. Buchanan and his hacker gang sent out hundreds of SMS messages to the mobile phones of people who worked for large tech or telecoms companies. The SMS phishing messages contained links to spoof websites designed to look like legitimate sites of victim companies. The group used messages like “Hi, your account is due to expire – you need to log in to your work account here immediately or you will lose access to work apps”. The websites then lured the recipient into providing confidential information, including personal identifying information (PII), and account usernames and passwords. The boys and young men did it on an industrial scale with Buchanan setting up a Telegram bot to collect all the victims’ credentials as the duped workers unwittingly handed over their login details. For some victim companies, subsequently stolen information included confidential work information, intellectual property, plus account access credentials, names, email addresses, and telephone numbers. The group then used stolen information and SIM-swapping techniques to target cryptocurrency investors in the United States. In the largest single theft, prosecutors said one victim lost $1.67m in December 2022. Overall, authorities calculated that Buchanan and his co-conspirators stole more than $11.6m from victims. Threatened with a blowtorch Buchanan was also a victim of cyber-criminals. In early 2023 his online identity and home address were leaked by rival hackers seeking access to his cryptocurrency. Cyber security researchers and journalists reported that he was assaulted at his home and threatened with a blowtorch. “TylerB and his group were highly sophisticated and organised but the violence he and others experienced was a sign of the troubling direction of these online communities of young hackers” says cyber security researcher Allison Nixon from Unit221B. Buchanan then reportedly fled to Canada to escape further threats before returning home. In April 2023, officers from Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom after receiving a request from the FBI. Investigators recovered a device containing the names and addresses of hacking victims, along with cryptocurrency seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim. The following month, Buchanan left the UK again. He was arrested on 31 May 2024 at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain while attempting to board a private flight to Naples. After being extradited to the United States, he remained in custody before being sentenced this week. In his November 2023 charge, Buchanan was named along with four American men and boys in their twenties and teens for alleged activity linked to the notorious cyber-criminal collective Scattered Spider. They have all pleaded guilty too and are now serving time in jail. Two other members of the Scattered Spider group were jailed in the UK in July for various cyber attacks including a disruptive one against Transport for London that caused £39m of damage.

items.title: Hakeem Jeffries, premier président noir de la Chambre des représentants aux États-Unis!
items.description: Désigné par les élus démocrates avec 251 voix contre 11, mercredi 18 novembre 2026, Hakeem Jeffries pourrait inscrire son nom dans l’histoire politique américaine. Sauf surprise lors du vote officiel du 3 janvier prochain, le député de New York deviendra le premier Afro-Américain à accéder à la présidence de la Chambre des représentants, dans un contexte marqué par des divisions au sein de son parti et des tensions avec Donald Trump. Le Parti démocrate américain s'apprête à franchir un cap historique. Son chef de file à la Chambre des représentants, Hakeem Jeffries, 56 ans, a été choisi mercredi 18 novembre par ses pairs pour prendre les rênes de cette institution à partir du 3 janvier prochain. Selon des informations rapportées par des médias, Hakeem a obtenu 251 suffrages contre 11 lors d'un vote à huis clos, sans véritable concurrent, mais non sans contestation au sein de son propre camp. Cette désignation ouvre la voie à une première historique. Si sa candidature est confirmée par la majorité des membres de la Chambre lors du scrutin officiel, le parlementaire de Brooklyn deviendra le premier homme noir à occuper ce prestigieux fauteuil, plus de 150 ans après l'entrée du premier élu afro-américain au Congrès des États-Unis. Il exercera cette responsabilité durant les deux dernières années du mandat de Donald Trump. À la suite de sa victoire, Hakeem Jeffries a mis en avant la nécessité de préserver la cohésion de son parti, malgré la diversité des sensibilités qui le composent. Il a salué la collaboration entre les élus démocrates, soulignant leur volonté commune de rechercher des compromis pour répondre aux préoccupations des Américains. Mais derrière ce succès électoral se dessinent des fractures persistantes. Onze représentants ont refusé de soutenir sa candidature. Parmi eux figurent des élus de la mouvance progressiste, qui lui reprochent notamment une opposition jugée insuffisamment ferme à Donald Trump et des positions favorables à Israël. D'autres contestent l'influence des grandes fortunes et des financements privés dans le fonctionnement des campagnes électorales, appelant à des changements structurels. Face à ces critiques, le futur président de la Chambre a exhorté les démocrates à ne pas transformer leurs divergences en affrontements internes. «Notre rôle est de combattre l'extrémisme MAGA, pas de nous combattre les uns les autres», a-t-il insisté, réaffirmant son engagement à défendre les intérêts de la population américaine et à faire avancer les réformes. La future équipe dirigeante devrait également compter Katherine Clark, pressentie pour devenir cheffe de la majorité, ainsi que Pete Aguilar, appelé à occuper les fonctions de chef de file de la majorité parlementaire. Tous deux ont été désignés sans opposition. Leur accession à ces responsabilités constituerait également des avancées symboliques puisque Clark serait la première femme à occuper ce poste, tandis qu'Aguilar deviendrait le premier élu latino-américain à diriger la majorité à la Chambre. Les défis qui attendent cette nouvelle équipe s'annoncent considérables. Les démocrates entendent notamment multiplier les enquêtes parlementaires sur les activités de l'administration Trump. Une perspective qui laisse présager de nouveaux bras de fer avec la Maison-Blanche, d'autant que le président américain a déjà brandi la menace de son veto contre les textes contraires à ses orientations politiques. Né à Brooklyn, Hakeem Jeffries a d'abord exercé comme avocat avant de faire ses premiers pas en politique à l'Assemblée de l'État de New York, où il a été élu en 2007. Il a ensuite rejoint le Congrès en 2013. Depuis 2022, il dirige les démocrates à la Chambre des représentants, après avoir succédé à Nancy Pelosi. Au-delà de la portée historique de cette possible accession, Hakeem Jeffries devra surtout transformer cette victoire en un véritable levier politique. Entre la nécessité de ressouder un camp divisé et la confrontation annoncée avec Donald Trump, son éventuelle présidence s'annonce comme un exercice d'équilibriste au cœur de la vie politique américaine. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Hakeem Jeffries, premier président noir de la Chambre des représentants aux États-Unis! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Here’s the latest.
COP31 draft proposes at least $120 billion annually for climate adaptation by 2035
items.description: A draft climate decision prepared under the COP31 Presidency has proposed increasing international adaptation finance for developing countries to at least US$120 billion annually by 2035, as concerns grow over the widening gap between the resources available and the cost of responding to climate change. The proposal forms part of a Presidency-led, Party-driven cover decision dated November 16, 2026, which outlines areas for collective action under the Paris Agreement. The document calls on developed countries to urgently increase their collective provision of adaptation finance and provide a roadmap explaining how the proposed target would be achieved. It also requests the development of a time-bound implementation pathway, including a clear baseline, milestones and arrangements for monitoring, reporting and reviewing progress. The proposal comes against the background of a substantial difference between estimated adaptation needs and available international public funding. Citing the United Nations Environment Programme’s 2026 Adaptation Gap Report, the draft puts annual adaptation finance needs in developing countries at approximately US$305 billion by 2035. However, international public adaptation finance stood at between US$28 billion and US$32 billion in 2024, only US$1 billion more than the previous year. The document further notes that even tripling adaptation finance by 2035 would cover no more than 29 per cent of estimated needs. It therefore calls for increased financial support, particularly for least developed countries, small island developing states and other developing countries facing significant capacity constraints. Calls for action on fossil fuels The draft also takes a position on fossil fuels, calling for accelerated action to phase them out, including through an immediate transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems. It reaffirms the call for countries to transition away from fossil fuels in a just, orderly and equitable manner, while emphasising the need to phase out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies that do not address energy poverty or just transitions. The document also calls for faster development and deployment of renewable energy, improved energy efficiency and modernisation of electricity grids. It proposes that countries contribute, according to their national circumstances, to global efforts to increase electricity’s share of total final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035. This is to be pursued alongside efforts to triple global renewable energy capacity and double the global average annual rate of energy efficiency improvements by 2030. The draft recognises that access to affordable and reliable energy remains important, particularly for developing economies and countries across Africa. Developing countries raise concerns over trade restrictions Another significant proposal concerns unilateral climate-related trade measures imposed by countries. The draft expresses serious concern that such measures could transfer the economic burden of climate action to other countries, particularly developing economies. It identifies potential consequences for market access, competitiveness, investment and industrialisation. It consequently calls on developed countries to phase out unilateral climate-related and trade-restrictive measures, as well as other measures with negative effects on international climate cooperation, by the end of 2027. The document also proposes developing common guiding principles for climate-related trade measures, including non-discrimination, transparency and interoperability. It asks for further discussions under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) to identify ways of avoiding, minimising and eliminating measures that adversely affect developing countries. Concerns over the 1.5°C target The draft acknowledges that global efforts remain insufficient to keep the 1.5°C temperature limit within reach. It expresses concern over scientific findings on temperature overshoot and recognises that every additional increment of warming increases the frequency and intensity of climate-related losses and damage. These impacts, it says, could include irreversible damage to human and natural systems, as well as increased risks of crossing climate tipping points. The document calls for efforts to return global warming to below 1.5°C as early as possible within this century. It also proposes establishing a scientific work programme to examine the evidence surrounding temperature overshoot, including ways to limit its magnitude and duration and respond to its consequences. The proposed programme would include annual dialogues and synthesis reports, with the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) informing the discussions. Climate finance access and loss and damage Beyond the proposed adaptation finance target, the draft highlights difficulties developing countries face in accessing international climate funding. It identifies high borrowing costs, limited fiscal space, unsustainable debt levels, transaction costs and funding conditions as barriers to financing climate action. It calls for increased grant-based, highly concessional and non-debt-creating finance. The document also proposes simpler and faster approval and disbursement procedures for climate funds, alongside greater direct access for national, subnational and regional institutions. On loss and damage, it notes that requests under the Barbados Implementation Modalities amount to approximately US$2.8 billion, compared with allocations of approximately US$342 million. It further states that only 50 per cent of the US$822 million pledged to the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage had reportedly been converted into contributions. The draft calls for increased resources for the institutions supporting countries affected by climate-related losses and damage. Early warning systems and climate resilience The document also places emphasis on strengthening early warning systems, recognising their role in saving lives, reducing losses and improving countries’ ability to prepare for climate-related hazards. It reaffirms the objective of achieving universal coverage of early warning systems by 2027 through the Early Warnings for All initiative. The draft calls for increased international support for developing countries, including funding, technology transfer, technical assistance and capacity-building. It also proposes integrating climate information and early warning systems into public health protection, disaster risk reduction and national adaptation planning. The document recognises that climate change is already affecting human health through heat stress, climate-sensitive diseases, food and nutrition insecurity and damage to health facilities during extreme weather events. It identifies malaria, dengue and cholera among the diseases through which climate change can affect public health. What happens next? The proposals are contained in an unedited negotiating text prepared under COP31 Presidency consultations. They cover climate finance, mitigation, adaptation, energy, trade, health, oceans, biodiversity and international cooperation. Several provisions also leave room for further negotiations. For example, the document requests additional work to establish the baseline and implementation arrangements for the proposed adaptation finance target. The text also contains alternative wording on aspects of the proposed follow-up to the Belém Mission to 1.5, indicating that these provisions have not yet been settled. The proposals therefore remain subject to negotiations among the parties before any final decision can be established on November 20, 2026.

items.title: Minority MPs question government’s economic claims after Techiman market tour
items.description: Minority MPs have taken their assessment of Ghana’s economy to the Techiman Central Market and lorry terminals, saying early interactions with traders and transport operators raise questions about the government’s positive outlook ahead of the 2027 Budget debate. The delegation, led by Nsawam Adoagyire MP Annor Dompreh, said it was engaging market participants to understand how economic conditions and government policies were affecting businesses and households. Speaking to the media during the tour on Thursday, November 19, 2026, Mr Dompreh said the team had heard concerns about the cost of living and the operating expenses facing transport operators. “Cost of living, transport owners are complaining about the ex-pump price of petrol, price of spare parts, and its attendant effect on cost of living. That is what we are taking and it’s almost becoming a trend and it’s reflecting in the local economy,” he said. Mr Dompreh said the Minority was not convinced that the government’s claims of economic improvement fully reflected conditions experienced by ordinary Ghanaians. “I am not saying the economy is good. The cost of living has improved. We have our doubts. That’s why we are here to speak to our people and to hear from them. It simply is the purpose of this visit,” he said. He argued that markets and other local trading centres offered an important perspective on the impact of government policies and budget decisions. “We believe that the reflection of what the budget is and the effect of the budget is in our markets. The local settings is where the real economy is. So, we are here to interact with our people and to get the facts,” he said. The Nsawam Adoagyire MP also defended the decision to conduct the exercise in Techiman, describing the town as an important commercial centre whose economic conditions should feature in national assessments. “Techiman is part of Ghana. Techiman is equally part of Ghana. Ghana is not Accra. And you know, Parliament is located in Accra and often times, we overly concentrate on these matters in Accra. But Techiman is strategic in terms of commerce,” he said. “Besides the point, Techiman is also part of Ghana. So, I also ask the same question. Why not Techiman? So, it’s equally important,” he added. The tour comes as Parliament debates the 2027 Budget Statement, which projects economic growth of 5.2% for 2027. The government has cited its New Economy plan and the Big Push infrastructure programme as part of its strategy to drive economic growth. The Minority has criticised the budget, describing it as a repackaged version of the 24-Hour Economy policy. The delegation is expected to use feedback gathered from the market and lorry terminals to inform its contributions to the budget debate.

items.title: “Stop abusing students” – GES PRO on UGEL’s GH¢8,000 Hostel fee
items.description: The Public Relations Officer of the Ghana Education Service (GES), Daniel Fenyi, has taken issue with the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) over its reported GH¢8,000 annual hostel fee per student, describing the charge as exploitative. He has consequently called for a rethink of how university education is delivered in Ghana. Mr Fenyi argued that charging GH¢8,000 per student for a four-in-a-room hostel translates into GH¢32,000 annually for a single room, an amount he believes places an excessive financial burden on students and their families. In a Facebook post, he said the controversy surrounding university accommodation should prompt a wider national discussion about alternative and more affordable ways of accessing higher education. “Charging GH¢8,000 per student for a four-in-a-room hostel, amounting to GH¢32,000 a year for a single room, is very exploitative. Stop abusing students,” he wrote. His comments come amid a disagreement between UGEL and Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku, following the latter’s attempt to inspect university-managed hostels over concerns about accommodation charges and the condition of some facilities. The development has brought renewed attention to the cost of student accommodation, the responsibilities of hostel operators and the regulation of university-managed residential facilities. Beyond the immediate controversy over hostel charges, Mr Fenyi believes the situation presents an opportunity for universities to reconsider the traditional model of delivering higher education, particularly the emphasis on physical attendance and residential accommodation. He called for universities to expand distance education, online and virtual learning, sandwich programmes and modular courses, arguing that such arrangements could reduce students’ dependence on campus accommodation while making tertiary education more accessible. According to him, several programmes in the humanities, arts, education and business could be delivered through flexible learning arrangements without compromising academic standards. He maintained that universities must take advantage of technological advancements to widen access to higher education and ease the financial pressures students face when relocating to other parts of the country to pursue their studies. “I believe there is an urgent need for deliberate, large-scale technological disruption in the way we deliver higher education in this country,” he stated. While advocating greater adoption of virtual learning, Mr Fenyi acknowledged that not all university programmes could be delivered entirely online. He noted that courses involving laboratory experiments, clinical practice, studio sessions and other intensive practical components would still require appropriate face-to-face instruction. However, he argued that many other academic programmes could be organised around virtual classes, weekend sessions, distance learning and modular arrangements, giving students greater flexibility in pursuing their degrees. He pointed to the University of Cape Coast (UCC), the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA) and other institutions that have introduced postgraduate programmes designed for fully virtual delivery. Describing the developments as encouraging, he urged universities to consider extending similar arrangements to undergraduate programmes to accommodate a wider range of students. Questions traditional model of university education Mr Fenyi also challenged the long-held assumption that obtaining a university degree must necessarily involve relocating to another town, competing for limited hostel spaces and paying increasingly expensive accommodation fees. He argued that access to quality higher education should not be determined by a student’s ability to secure accommodation or meet the rising cost of living near a university campus. “Most definitely, we must begin to question the assumption that obtaining a university degree must necessarily mean physically relocating to another town, competing for scarce accommodation and falling prey to hostellers charging unreasonable rent fees,” he wrote. He called on universities to rethink their existing delivery models and adopt more inclusive approaches that would allow students from different financial backgrounds to pursue higher education without the additional burden of securing residential accommodation. He further urged the government, regulators and other stakeholders to establish the necessary policies and institutional structures to support the expansion of flexible, accessible and technology-driven learning across the tertiary education sector. “Higher education must become more accessible, flexible and technology driven. A university education should not come with an accommodation crisis as part of the admission package,” he stressed. He urged the government, regulators and other key stakeholders to put the necessary policies and structures in place to make higher education more accessible, flexible and responsive to technological advancements.

items.title: Mohamed Ouattara quitte la tête de l’IGT : « Un poste n’appartient à personne… »
items.description: La passation de service entre l'inspecteur général du travail sortant, Mohamed Ouattara, et son successeur, Dr Baba Nabé, s'est tenue dans la matinée de ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026, sous la présidence de la ministre de l'Emploi, du Travail et de la Protection sociale, Ramatoulaye Camara. Cette cérémonie, marquant un changement à la tête de l'Inspection générale du travail, a été l'occasion de dresser le bilan des réformes engagées, de présenter les chantiers en cours et de définir les nouvelles orientations de l'institution, notamment en matière de contrôle des entreprises, de protection des travailleurs et de dialogue social. Prenant la parole à cette occasion, l'inspecteur général sortant, Mohamed Ouattara, a exprimé sa reconnaissance au président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, ainsi qu'aux différents responsables gouvernementaux qui lui ont accordé leur confiance depuis sa nomination, le 19 juillet 2024. « Un poste, il n'appartient à personne. On le reçoit comme un dépôt, on le sert avec loyauté, on le quitte avec classe, on le transmet avec sérénité et dignité », a-t-il déclaré, insistant sur le caractère temporaire des responsabilités publiques et la nécessité de préserver la continuité du service de l'État. Revenant sur les acquis enregistrés durant ses deux années à la tête de l'institution, il a notamment mis en avant la transformation numérique de l'Inspection générale du travail. Il a cité la mise en place de la plateforme numérique Digita, conçue et développée par ses soins, avec la contribution des équipes de l'inspection, pour faciliter et moderniser les opérations de contrôle sur le terrain. Il a également révélé que les activités de l'institution ont permis de générer 3 milliards 722 millions 607 mille francs guinéens, désormais enregistrés sur un compte ouvert au Trésor public. À ces résultats, il a ajouté le renforcement des moyens logistiques et matériels, précisant que tous les inspecteurs régionaux du travail disposent désormais de véhicules et que les 159 inspecteurs et contrôleurs du travail sont équipés de tablettes pour effectuer des contrôles digitalisés. Il a également évoqué la mise en application de l'obligation de déclaration et de certification du bilan social des entreprises. « Ce bilan n'est pas celui d'un homme, c'est celui d'une équipe qui a accepté de travailler plus avec peu, parce qu'elle croyait à sa mission », a-t-il souligné, saluant l'engagement et la disponibilité de ses collaborateurs. Toutefois, il a tenu à attirer l'attention de son successeur sur plusieurs dossiers prioritaires. Parmi ceux-ci figurent le processus de recrutement de 135 inspecteurs et contrôleurs du travail, dont les résultats ont été transmis à la hiérarchie, la réalisation d'une enquête sur les risques psychosociaux en milieu professionnel ainsi que le suivi de plusieurs dossiers contentieux sensibles. Il a également relevé la persistance de difficultés liées à l'insuffisance des effectifs et aux moyens logistiques, au regard du nombre d'entreprises nécessitant un contrôle régulier sur l'ensemble du territoire national. S'adressant à son successeur, il a insisté sur la nécessité de préserver les acquis et de s'appuyer sur les compétences disponibles au sein de l'institution. « Aujourd'hui, vous épousez une très belle femme. Cette femme aujourd'hui, elle a les moyens de payer sa dot, c'est l'Inspection générale du travail. Je vous prie d'en prendre soin », a-t-il lancé dans une métaphore destinée à inviter son successeur à prendre soin de l'institution et de ses collaborateurs. De son côté, le nouvel inspecteur général du travail, Dr Baba Nabé, a exprimé sa reconnaissance au chef de l'État pour la confiance placée en lui, tout en mesurant l'ampleur des responsabilités qui accompagnent cette nomination. Dans son intervention, il a rappelé le rôle stratégique de l'Inspection générale du travail dans l'application de la législation sociale, le contrôle des conditions d’emploi, la prévention des risques professionnels et la conciliation des différends entre employeurs et travailleurs. Évoquant les priorités du gouvernement, il a particulièrement insisté sur les enjeux liés à la création d’emplois pour les jeunes et les femmes, qui doivent, selon lui, s'accompagner du respect des dispositions légales et de garanties en matière de santé et de sécurité au travail. Le déploiement du programme Simandou 2040 constitue également, à ses yeux, un enjeu majeur pour l'institution. Il a annoncé que les contrôles devront accorder une attention particulière aux conditions d’emploi sur les grands chantiers, au respect des règles relatives à l’emploi des travailleurs étrangers et à la prévention des risques professionnels, y compris au niveau des entreprises sous-traitantes. Le nouveau patron de l'Inspection générale du travail entend également renforcer les interventions dans les préfectures afin de rendre les services de l'institution plus accessibles aux travailleurs et aux employeurs. Sur le plan méthodologique, Dr Baba Nabé a promis une application rigoureuse et impartiale de la législation du travail, fondée sur des faits établis, le respect des procédures et des décisions motivées. « Je veillerai au strict respect de la législation du travail avec la même exigence à l'égard de tous », a-t-il affirmé. Il a par ailleurs annoncé des rencontres avec les équipes des services centraux et des inspections régionales afin d'évaluer les dossiers en instance, d'identifier les secteurs nécessitant davantage de contrôles et de déterminer les besoins en formation, en équipements et en moyens de déplacement. Le renforcement du dialogue social figure également parmi ses engagements. À ce titre, il a assuré les organisations syndicales et patronales de sa disponibilité, tout en promettant un traitement impartial des différends et un meilleur suivi des engagements pris lors des conciliations. Saluant le travail accompli par son prédécesseur, il a notamment cité sa contribution aux travaux sur la convention collective des mines et carrières, les médiations conduites sur les sites miniers ainsi que les efforts engagés pour renforcer les contrôles et digitaliser les activités de l'inspection. Prenant la parole pour fixer le cap de la nouvelle équipe, la ministre de l'Emploi, du Travail et de la Protection sociale, Ramatoulaye Camara, a rappelé le caractère stratégique de l'Inspection générale du travail dans la mise en œuvre de la politique gouvernementale en matière d’emploi et de protection des travailleurs. Elle a d'abord salué les efforts de l'équipe sortante, tout en insistant sur la nécessité de préserver les acquis et de poursuivre les réformes engagées. « Dans l'administration publique, les responsabilités évoluent et les équipes se renouvellent. À chaque passation, la continuité du service nous oblige à transmettre les dossiers avec rigueur, à préserver les acquis et à poursuivre les engagements pris au service de nos populations », a-t-elle indiqué. S'adressant au nouvel inspecteur général, elle a appelé à une application stricte du Code du travail et des textes régissant les relations professionnelles en Guinée. Elle a notamment demandé à la nouvelle équipe de multiplier les contrôles dans les entreprises, aussi bien sur les grands chantiers que dans les petites structures, à Conakry comme à l'intérieur du pays. Une attention particulière devra être accordée aux situations présentant des risques pour la santé et la sécurité des travailleurs. La ministre a également insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer les moyens d'intervention des services centraux et des inspections régionales, afin de leur permettre d'accomplir efficacement leurs missions sur toute l'étendue du territoire national. Abordant la question du dialogue social, elle a rappelé que l'Inspection générale du travail doit demeurer un cadre accessible aux travailleurs et aux employeurs, tout en entretenant des relations régulières avec les organisations syndicales et patronales. Enfin, elle a invité le nouveau patron de l'IGT à établir rapidement ses premières priorités, à assurer le suivi des dossiers transmis par son prédécesseur et à rendre compte régulièrement des résultats obtenus ainsi que des difficultés nécessitant un arbitrage de la hiérarchie. « Un décret nous engage. Quand on accepte une responsabilité, ce sont des sacrifices qui vont avec », a-t-elle rappelé, avant de souligner que la rigueur attendue des responsables doit également s'appliquer à eux-mêmes. Youssouf Keita L’article Mohamed Ouattara quitte la tête de l’IGT : « Un poste n’appartient à personne… » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: DPM Dar, Asean secretary general agree to enhance cooperation to address ‘non-traditional’ security challenges
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Secretary General of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Dr Kao Kim Hourn agreed to enhance cooperation in addressing “non-traditional” security challenges on Thursday. Addressing a joint press stakeout with Hourn after delegation-level talks held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, DPM Dar said that the discussions had focused on strengthening political, economic and socio-cultural cooperation. “We agreed to enhance cooperation in addressing non-traditional security challenges, including climate change, food insecurity, disruptions to energy supplies and cyber threats,” he said. “Our ability to respond to these challenges together is vital to the security of our people and the sustainability of our development.” Dar added that the two sides had discussed ways to expand cooperation in trade, education, technology, climate change and food security while promoting cultural and people-to-people exchanges. He stressed that economic cooperation was central to their discussions, including facilitating trade, improving connectivity and enhancing digital integration, with a focus on creating more opportunities for businesses and strengthening the links between Asean and Pakistan’s markets. “Building on the Asean-Pakistan business conferences, we look forward to partnerships that connect businesses, open new markets and create more jobs,” he said. The two sides also discussed strengthening links between universities and research institutions in order to encourage joint research, exchange of expertise and skill development, particularly in digital technologies and artificial intelligence; as well as to increase cultural, academic and youth exchanges. They also discussed regional and international security, the deputy premier said, highlighting Asean’s role in promoting dialogue and regional integration at a time of growing political uncertainty and an evolving geopolitical landscape, including by bringing countries together around shared interests. “Pakistan values this approach and looks forward to closer engagement with Asean to advance peace and shared prosperity,” Dar said. He stressed the importance of secure sea routes and uninterrupted supply chains for economies and livelihoods, adding that the two leaders reaffirmed the central role of dialogue and diplomacy, respect for international law and adherence to the United Nations Charter in addressing challenges and expressing Pakistan’s continued engagement with key partners in this regard. He also expressed concern over the continued expansion of illegal settlements in the West Bank, calling for unhindered humanitarian assistance to be delivered to Gaza and reiterating his support for an independent Palestinian state. Regarding the situation in South Asia, he also briefed Hourn on the importance of “a just, durable and peaceful settlement of the longstanding Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions”, while also expressing concern over India’s unilateral decision to hold the Indus Water Treaty in abeyance, threatening water, food and energy security for Pakistan. He also highlighted Pakistan’s concern over the continued use of Afghan soil for carrying out terrorist attacks. DPM Dar said that Hourn’s visit — the first by an Asean secretary general in over two decades — offered an opportunity to build on the close friendly ties between Pakistan and Asean. “We look forward to giving fresh impetus to our partnership through practical cooperation that benefits our people,” he said. Hourn, during his address, underscored the potential to deepen Pakistan-Asean relations in the areas of economic cooperation, regional peace and security, and people-to-people connectivity, translating their longstanding relationship into “more substantive cooperation and tangible benefits”. He called for stronger connections between the business communities and noted promising opportunities in the renewable energy sector, as well as the potential to deepen cooperation against shared international challenges including terrorism, violent extremism, human trafficking and international crime. “I would encourage Pakistan to make greater use of Asean’s various centres and institutions as a platform for capacity building, technical cooperation and knowledge sharing, drawing on experience and expertise available between our two sides,” he said. In addition, he welcomed Pakistan’s constructive role in facilitating negotiations between the US and Iran, which resulted in the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June, and acknowledged the country’s efforts to facilitate dialogue and de-escalation. Hourn is on a working visit to Pakistan from November 18 to 20. In their delegation-level talks, the two sides reviewed progress under the Pakistan-Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partnership, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a post on X. According to the handout, the discussions between the two sides focused on expanding trade and investment, strengthening regional connectivity, and deepening cooperation in agriculture and food security. Collaboration on climate resilience, disaster preparedness, and digital innovation also came under discussion. During the talks, DPM Dar stressed the scope for closer links between the business communities of Pakistan and Asean member states as well as the significance of scholarships, student exchanges, and joint research to strengthen people-to-people ties. The FO added that the two sides also exchanged views on regional developments and appreciated Pakistan’s “constructive role” in promoting regional peace and stability. DPM Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to working closely with the Asean Secretariat and member states to advance the partnership. Separately, the secretary general called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, where they discussed ways to enhance trade, investment and economic cooperation and expand collaboration in food security, climate change, IT and education, the FO said. PM Shehbaz underscored the importance of “translating the existing goodwill into concrete economic and development partnerships”, highlighting Pakistan’s strategic location at the crossroads of Central Asia, the Middle East and West Asia and its potential as a gateway for the wider region. Hourn “reaffirmed Asean’s commitment to strengthening relations with Pakistan, welcomed Pakistan’s interest in closer engagement, and expressed confidence that continued cooperation and the visit would help advance the partnership”, the FO added. A day earlier, the FO had said Hourn’s arrival marked the first high-level visit to Pakistan from the Asean Secretariat. Pakistan has been an Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner since 1993, and a member of the Asean Regional Forum since 2004, it added. Asean was founded on August 8, 1967, when Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand signed the Bangkok Declaration, setting goals for economic and other types of cooperation and regional peace and stability. The bloc has 11 members, including Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia, and East Timor. “The visit underscores Pakistan and Asean’s shared commitment to deepening and diversifying cooperation,” FO said in its Wednesday statement. Earlier this year, Dar attended the 33rd Ministerial Meeting of the Asean Regional Forum in Manila, where he drew attention to key challenges threatening peaceful coexistence and stability across the world, listing the Kashmir dispute and India’s threats to Pakistan’s share of water among them. Last year, seven Asean member countries held a joint meeting with Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh to explore new avenues of investment and economic cooperation with Pakistan.

items.title: Ibrahim Mbaye, Lion le plus décisif en sélection depuis ses débuts
items.description: Le 15 novembre 2025, Ibrahim Mbaye honorait sa 1re sélection avec le Sénégal. Un an plus tard, l’ailier est (déjà) devenu un maillon essentiel des Lions. Retour sur une année formidable pour le gamin de 18 ans qui tutoie déjà les sommets. Le 15 novembre 2025 est à marquer d’une pierre blanche pour Ibrahim Mbaye. Certes, le Sénégal avait perdu 0-2 en amical contre le Brésil, match durant lequel l’ancien Parisien n’a disputé « que » 15 minutes. Mais l’ailier virevoltant débutait son aventure avec les Lions, honorant sa première sélection. Trois jours plus tard, contre le Kenya, Pape Thiaw, ancien sélectionneur du Sénégal, lui offrait sa première titularisation. L’occasion pour la pépite de démontrer toute l’étendue de son talent et au Sénégal de découvrir un véritable diamant. Résultat des courses : 1 but, 2 passes décisives et un succès 8-0. Un an plus tard, Ibrahim Mbaye compte déjà 20 sélections, alors qu’il n’a même pas fêté ses 19 ans (il les fêtera en janvier). Son bilan statistique est tout simplement exceptionnel : il est crédité par des analystes statistiques comme Transfermarkt de 6 buts et de 6 passes décisives. Précocité jamais vue C’est simple, ces performances font d’Ibrahim Mbaye le joueur le plus décisif en sélection depuis ses débuts. Avec 12 contributions, il devance Nicolas Jackson sur la période (8 buts, 3 passes décisives), Sadio Mané (7 buts, 3 passes décisives) et Ismaïla Sarr (5 buts, 3 passes décisives). Lors de la CAN 2025 remportée par le Sénégal au Maroc, Mbaye a joué un rôle déterminant en sortie de banc, devenant, à 17 ans et 344 jours, le plus jeune buteur sénégalais en Coupe d’Afrique et le plus jeune Africain à scorer dans la compétition au XXIe siècle. Lors du Mondial 2026, son but contre la France lui a permis de devenir le plus jeune buteur africain de l’histoire en Coupe du monde, à 18 ans et 143 jours. Lorsqu’il débarquait en sélection, les observateurs attendaient un pari pour l’avenir. Mais Ibrahim Mbaye est déjà un maillon essentiel pour les Lions, à seulement 18 ans, annonçant un avenir radieux. Oumar Bounacar NDONGO

items.title: Airspace ban on Indian aircraft extended till Dec 24
items.description: Pakistan has extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft until Dec 24, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA). The previous extension of the ban was set to expire on Nov 24. “Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights,” the Notam said. According to the notice, the ban will remain in place until 04:59am PST on Dec 24 (23:59pm UTC on Dec 23). The country’s airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs) — Karachi and Lahore, according to a Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document from 2022. The Notam applies to both the Karachi (OPKR) and Lahore (OPLR) FIRs. India and Pakistan closed their airspaces to each other’s airlines in late April 2025, when tensions between them escalated in the wake of a deadly attack in India-occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam. On April 24, Pakistan’s top brass announced a series of measures , including the closure of its airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines with immediate effect, as it retaliated against New Delhi’s slew of aggressive measures against the country. New Delhi, without evidence, had alleged that Islamabad backed the Pahalgam attack. However, Pakistan had strongly denied any involvement and offered a neutral probe . The nuclear powers had the fiercest air battle in May, in which Pakistan said it downed seven Indian fighter jets. Since then, Pakistan has extended the airspace ban several times, forcing Indian carriers to use longer and costlier routes. For Air India, the country’s only carrier with a major international network, fuel costs rose by as much as 29 per cent and journey times by up to three hours on some long-haul routes, according to a document submitted to Indian officials last October. The airline, owned by Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, estimated the Pakistan airspace closure’s impact on its profit before tax at $455 million annually — a significant amount given its fiscal 2024-25 loss stood at $439m.
